text: Acute febrile illness, progressive. BM smear for Tryp. rh. +/-, LP pending. Dx: rhodesiense trypano, unsp. Rule out meningitis. Start IV melarsoprol 1.2mg/kg qd x 7, then 2.2mg/kg qd x 7. F/u labs in 48h.

FC: 28F, b/f seizures for 1 wk. c/o h/a, nausea. CT head shows 3 ring-enhancing lesions, no hydrocephalus. Labs: CSF sent for cell count, Xpert for TB. Pt sent for MRI. Plan: start ABZ, phenytoin. Dx: Cysticercosis CNS, unspecified. Hx: DM2.

நோயாளி 52 வயது ஆண், காய்ச்சல், தசைவலி, தலைவலி. H/O விடுதியில் தங்கியிருந்தபோது ஈற்றி கொசு கடித்தது. WCC 5.2, Hb 11.8, Plat 140k. Peripheral smear (thin & thick) +ve for falciparum, no complications. TTP 48h. Start full course ACT (artemether-lumefantrine). Advise LFT monitoring.

A/O 14M. छाmeasurement, जिनका 7 दिन पहले टिक बाइट था। अब 2nd-degree AV ब्लॉक (Wenckebach), हल्का हार्ट फेलियर। Lyme serology IgM+, IgG+, 3D बोरेलिया IgM+। कार्डियोलॉजी को रेफर किया। Doxycycline 100mg BID। 2 हफ्ते में टेलीमेडिसिन फॉलो-अप।

Doctor: Good morning. So what brings you in today?
Patient: It's my stomach. Been feeling off for maybe three weeks now. I work in construction, and we poured a lot of concrete recently, but I don't think it's that. The main thing is I can't seem to keep my weight up. I'm eating the same, maybe more, but the scale keeps dropping.
Doctor: Any nausea, or pain in your belly?
Patient: Some cramping, like after I eat. And I've been having loose motions, nothing bloody. Oh, and I noticed my stools look a bit dark, almost black, but I'm not passing any red blood.
Doctor: Any skin issues? Like a rash or itchy track on your feet?
Patient: No, my feet are fine. No rashes, no itching.
Doctor: And your travel history? I know you mentioned the construction site, but any recent trips abroad, especially to parts of the tropics?
Patient: Yeah, right before this started, I spent about two weeks at a community build in a rural area of the southeast. It was a volunteer thing.
Doctor: Okay, I'm worried this sounds like an intestinal worm infection. The black stools, the weight loss, and the cramping all point to blood loss in your gut. The fact that you were in that rural area really points to a specific type. I'd say you've got an infection from the New World hookworm. Are there any other symptoms, like shortness of breath or a cough?
Patient: No, no breathing issues, definitely no cough. I've been feeling weak though, tired all the time. I'm losing sleep because I feel like I'm starving.
Doctor: Right. The chronic blood loss is probably causing the iron deficiency anemia. I'm going to order a stool ova and parasite exam to confirm, and I'll start you on an antiparasitic today. Let's call it albendazole. I want you back in a few days to see how you feel after the first dose. Any questions?
Patient: Just, what is it exactly?
Doctor: It's a type of hookworm that causes intestinal blood loss, which is why your blood counts are low. We'll treat it today.

S: ৭২ বছর বয়সী মহিলাকে ৩ দিন ধরে বারবার জ্বর, মাথা ব্যথা, পেশীতে ব্যথা এবং কাঁপুনি নিয়ে ক্লিনিকে আনা হয়েছে। তিনি সম্প্রতি হরিয়ানা-রাজস্থানের বর্ডার এলাকায় তাঁবুতে camping করতে গিয়েছিলেন। সেখানে একটি পোকা কামড়ের ইতিহাস জানিয়েছেন, যা কিছুদিন আগে পড়ে গিয়েছিল। রোগীর কোনো গৃহহীনতা বা লম্বা সময় ধরে কাপড়ে না ধোয়ার ইতিহাস নেই।
O: ভাইটালস: তাপমাত্রা ৩৭.৫°C, রক্তচাপ ১২০/৮০ mmHg, হার্ট রেট ৯৫ bpm, রেসপিরেটরি রেট ১৮/মিনিট। শারীরিক পরীক্ষায়: মাঝারি ম্যালেরিয়া ধরনের রক্তাল্পতা (Hb ৯.৮ g/dL), হার্ট রেট ১০৫ bpm। পেরিফেরাল স্মিয়ারে কোনো ম্যালেরিয়া পরজীবী বা স্পোরোজোয়েট দেখা যায়নি। ইএসআর ৬২ mm/hr, সি-রিঅ্যাকটিভ প্রোটিন ২১0 mg/L। ডব্লিউবিসি কাউন্ট ১০.২ x10^9/L। মেটাবলিক প্যানেল স্বাভাবিক। টিক-বোর্ন রিলেপসিং ফিভার (TBRF) এর জন্য পিসিআর টেস্ট অর্ডার করা হয়েছে। লেপ্টোস্পিরা, ডায়াসপার এবং ম্যালেরিয়া রুল আউট করা হয়েছে।
A: টিক-বোর্ন রিলেপসিং ফিভার (TBRF)।
P: ১. এমোক্সি-ক্ল্যাভ ৮৭৫/১২৫ mg দিনে দু'বার মুখে (PO BID) শুরু করা হলো।
২. ডিহাইড্রেশন এড়াতে মুখে তরল গ্রহণ বাড়াতে হবে (PO fluids)।
৩. ৪৮ ঘণ্টার মধ্যে পিসিআর রিপোর্ট এলে অ্যান্টিবায়োটিক পরিবর্তন করা হবে।
৪. আরআই-টিবি স্ক্রিনিং এবং Hb মনিটরিং করতে হবে।
৫. ফলো-আপ অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট ২ সপ্তাহ পরে নির্ধারণ করা হলো।

S: 68 yo F presents for worsening abdominal pain and intermittent diarrhea x 6 weeks. She reports recent travel to Southeast Asia and recent ingestion of undercooked freshwater fish. Denies fever, night sweats, or hematochezia. Prior history is notable for stable GERD. No prior parasitic infections.

O: Vitals stable. Abdominal exam reveals mild diffuse tenderness without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds active. Stool O&P sent from local lab returned with multiple ova and parasites. Microscopic examination identified Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, and Ancylostoma duodenale. Patient was asymptomatic for mild hypochromic anemia.

A: Mixed intestinal helminthiases. Documented polymicrobial adult GI nematode infection following epidemiological exposure. Patient is mildly anemic, likely multifactorial anemia from chronic B12 and iron deficiency.

P: 1. Start albendazole 400 mg daily for 3 days and ivermectin 200 mcg/kg once. 2. Schedule repeat stool O&P in 2 weeks to confirm clearance. 3. Counsel on food safety/hygiene and safe disposal of human feces. 4. Continue GERD regimen. 5. CBC in 2 weeks.

Doctor: Bonjour, je vois votre dossier. Vous avez présenté des plaques cutanées hypoesthésiques au niveau du coude droit. C'est un tableau classique, non ? Vous n'avez rien d'autre à signaler ? Pas de fièvre, pas de douleur à ce site ? Très bien. J'ai fait une biopsie de la lésion qui confirme une lèpre dite pauci-bacillaire. Ça correspond à la forme tuberculide, une forme limite. Les bacilles sont rares, donc votre immunité est encore de bonne tenue, ce qui explique l'absence de réaction ou de déficit neurologique pour l'instant. Le traitement est standard : vous allez prendre d'emblée une trithérapie combinant d'oxymycine, de rifampcine et de clofazimine pour douze mois. Il faut bien suivre le traitement. On vous aura fait un test d'urine pour exclure la lèpre multibacillaire, mais les résultats sont négatifs, donc c'est bien la forme pauci-bacillaire. Je vous revois dans un mois pour surveiller l'application du traitement et l'évolution des lésions. Avez-vous des questions ? Patient: Non, tout est clair. Merci Docteur.

5 साल का लड़का पिछले 3 दिन से बुखार और ठंड के साथ आया है। WBC 7.5, Hgb 8.2, प्लेटलेट्स 120k। स्मीयर में Babesia माइक्रोटी और HMB-2 पॉजिटिव दिखा। Travel history: पालतू कुत्ते के साथ खेलना। Doxy 100mg BID। माता-पिता को एप्रेक्सोनेटेड इन्फ्यूजन के लिए फॉलो-अप का निर्देश दिया।

Doctor: Good morning. So, today we are going to discuss the results from the anoscopy, which I performed last week. Patient: Okay. Doctor: Well, the biopsy from that area came back. It is confirmed to be a malignant neoplasm. That means it is a cancer. Patient: Cancer? Where exactly? Doctor: It is in the region of the anus or anal canal. Unfortunately, at this stage, we do not have a more specific subtype because the pathology report did not specify further. Patient: So, what does that mean for my treatment? Doctor: It means we will need to start staging workup to see if there is any spread, but as for the exact cell type, it is just classified as an unspecified malignant neoplasm in that area, so we will have to manage it based on those general findings. Patient: I see. Okay, so what is the next step?

S: Paciente de 68 años, mujer, refiere inicio gradual de edemas bilaterales en extremidades inferiores y dolor torácico intermitente de un mes de evolución. Deniega fiebre, pérdida de peso, trauma reciente ni antecedentes familiares de neoplasias. Admite hipertensión arterial no controlada y diabetes mellitus de estilo de vida. No toma tabaquismo ni alcohol.

O: Examen físico: edemas simétricos en tobillos y pantorrillas, sin eritema ni calor local. Auscultación pulmonar: rales finos en bases basales bilaterales; corazón sin murmullo. Abdomen blando y sin masas palpables. No se hallan lesiones cutáneas, ni hepatomegalia ni disritmias evidentes. Exámenes de laboratorio: Hb 10.2 g/dL, recuento normal, LDH elevada. Radiografía de tórax: cardiomegalia y probable infiltrado en bases. Ecocardiograma: paredes ventriculares normales sin masas intracardíacas ni derrame pericardial. Tomografía computarizada de abdomen y pelvis: sin masas hepáticas ni esplénicas identificables. Biopsia por punción percutánea de una lesión cutánea en pierna derecha: resultados inconclusos. Marcadores tumorales: CA-125 ligeramente elevado.

A: 1) Angiosarcoma, sinSITE_DEFINIR. Diagnóstico de neoplasia vascular de alto grado sin evidencia de afectación cardíaca, cutánea, mamaria o hepática en el momento del estudio. Se descartó miocardiopatía y otras entidades. 2) Síndrome de congestión venosa bilateral de extremidades inferiores. 3) Anemia de insuficiencia renal crónica. 4) Hipertensión arterial esencial.

P: 1) Derivar a Oncología Médica para evaluación de bioprótesis y estudios de imagen adicionales (RM de masas si se identifican). 2) Recetar enalapril 10 mg/día. 3) Dieta baja en sodio y restricción de líquidos. 4) Revisión en 2 semanas o antes de agravar.

Doctor: Bonjour, asseyez-vous. J'ai bien reçu les résultats de l'échographie abdominale que nous avions faite. Le radiologue a mis en évidence une lésion de 1,5 cm, bien délimitée, de type kyste sérothécifique, localisée dans le corps du pancréas. C'est une tumeur bénigne de l'endocrion pancréatique. Elle ne présente aucune caractéristique suggestive d'une tumeur maligne ni d'une muqueuse. Il n'y a pas de dilatation du canal de Wirsung. C'est une observation stable en comparaison avec l'examen datant de deux ans. Patient: Ah bon, pas de risque de cancer pour l'instant ? Doctor: Non, absolument pas. C'est une masse bénigne. Nous allons vous suivre tous les six mois avec une échographie pour s'assurer que ça ne grossit pas, mais rien ne vous inquiète. Patient: Et ça ne me cause pas de douleur ? Doctor: Non, vous n'avez pas mentionné de douleurs abdominales. C'est souvent asymptomatique, découverte par hasard. Patient: Très bien, je me sens rassuré. Doctor: Je vais vous faire une ordonnance pour une prise de sang hépatique cette semaine, pour vérifier la fonction pancréatique, mais tout va bien se passer. On vous revoit en six mois.

७५F. ४ महिने leukocytosis (WBC 28). स्प्लेनोमेगाली (spleen 12cm). परिधीय स्मीअर: डावीकडे सरकलेले न्यूक्लिअर लोब्स (shifted nuclei), कमी बेसोफिल्स, हाय लॅक्टेट डिहायड्रोजनेज. BCR-ABL1/FISH निगेटिव्ह. FBC/LFT, JAK2 V617F आणि CALR म्युटेशन चाचण्या निगेटिव्ह. Atypical CML (myeloproliferative neoplasm, BCR-ABL1-negative) सुचवले. फॉलो-अपसाठी हेमेटोलॉजीकडे संदर्भ. HNA साठी तपासणी.

Doctor: Bonjour, je suis le Dr. Lefevre. Je suis votre pédiatre. Qu'est-ce qui vous amène aujourd'hui?

Patient: Bonjour Docteur. Ma fille a un kyste abdominal. C'est sur son échographie. Elle a un peu de douleur sur le côté droit du ventre.

Doctor: Je vois. Elle est bien à jeun? Parlez-moi de ses mictions.

Patient: Elle a uriné dans son lit la nuit dernière, mais c'est rare. Sinon c'est normal.

D'après ses examens d'imagerie, il y a une masse qui touche l'uretère et la vessie de l'enfant. Nous n'avons pas de signes de métastase ni de tumeur maligne. Le scanner et l'IRM confirment que c'est une masse non-épithéliale. La biopsie est impossible pour le moment car elle est trop proche de l'uretère. Je vais la renvoyer chez un urologue pédiatrique pour un suivi de cette masse. Nous n'avons pas de tumeur suspecte de type carcinome, c'est juste une masse de comportement inconnu sur l'organe urinaire.

Patient: D'accord Docteur. Merci pour l'explication.

S: ৫৫ বছর বয়সী পুরুষ রোগী গত ৩ সপ্তাহ ধরে সাধারণ দুর্বলতা এবং ওজন কমার সমস্যায় ভুগছেন। কোনো স্পষ্ট ফোলা বা লিম্ফ নোডের সমস্যা নেই। জ্বর বা রাতের ঘাম নেই। কোনো পেট ব্যথা বা মলের সাথে রক্ত নেই। পেটে কোনো স্পষ্ট ভর নেই। 3 মাস আগে হঠাৎ করে জ্বর এসেছিল যা নিজে থেকেই সেরে যায়। 10 বছর আগে ক্রনিক হেপাটাইটিস বি (HBsAg পজিটিভ) ধরা পড়েছিল, যা বর্তমানে স্থিতিশীল। রোগী ধূমপান করেন না এবং মদ্যপান করেন না। পারিবারিক ইতিহাসে কোলোরেক্টাল ক্যান্সারের ইতিহাস রয়েছে (বাবা)।

O: ভাইটালস: বিপি ১২০/৮০, এইচআর ৮৫, টিপি ৯৮.৬°F, SpO2 ৯৯%। সাধারণ পরীক্ষায়: অ্যানিমিক কিন্তু জন্ডিস নেই। লিম্ফ নোড, স্প্লিন বা হেপাটোস্প্লেনোমেগালি-র কোনো ক্লিনিক্যাল প্রমাণ নেই। পেটের পরীক্ষা নরম এবং কোনো টেন্ডারনেস নেই। পূর্ণাঙ্গ রক্ত পরীক্ষায় দেখা গেছে: Hb ৮.৫ g/dL, WBC ১১.২ x10^9/L (উচ্চ), প্লেটলেট ৩৫০ x10^9/L। সিরাম ইমিউনোগ্লোবুলিন প্রোফাইলে কোনো স্পষ্ট বৃদ্ধি দেখা যায়নি। LDH স্বাভাবিক। CRP ১২ mg/L (হালকা বৃদ্ধি)। AFP এবং CEA স্বাভাবিক। হেপাটাইটিস ই প্যানেল নেগেটিভ। সিরাম প্রোটিন ইলেক্ট্রোফোরেসিস (SPEP) এবং ইমিউনোফিক্সেশনে কোনো M-spike বা মনোক্লোনাল প্রোটিন শনাক্ত হয়নি। মলের occult blood টেস্ট নেগেটিভ। পেটের আল্ট্রাসাউন্ড নরমাল। বুকের এক্স-রে পরিষ্কার। কোনো লিম্ফ নোড বায়োপসিতে অ্যাটিপিক্যাল লিম্ফোসাইট বা ভারী শৃঙ্খল রোগ (Heavy chain disease) এর কোনো হিস্টোলজিক্যাল প্রমাণ পাওয়া যায়নি। হেমাটোলজি রেফারেন্সে হেভি চেইন ডিজিজ, স্পেসিফাইড সাবটাইপ (যেমন- আলফা, গামা বা মিউ) এর কোনো প্রমাণ নেই।

A: ভারী শৃঙ্খল রোগ, অনির্দিষ্ট (Heavy chain disease, unspecified)। এটি একটি বিরল ম্যালিগন্যান্ট ইমিউনোপ্রোলিফারেটিভ ডিসঅর্ডার। বর্তমানে আনস্পেসিফাইড ক্যাটাগরিতে রাখা হচ্ছে কারণ ক্লিনিক্যাল এবং ল্যাবরেটরি পরীক্ষায় নির্দিষ্ট ভারী শৃঙ্খলের কোনো সাবটাইপ (অ্যালফা, গামা, বা মিউ) বা অন্য কোনো নির্দিষ্ট ম্যালিগন্যান্ট ইমিউনোপ্রোলিফারেটিভ রোগ শনাক্ত করা যায়নি।

P: ১. হেমাটোলজি এবং ওনকোলজির সাথে পরবর্তী আলোচনার জন্য রেফার করা হলো। প্রয়োজনে উন্নত ইমিউনোফেনোটাইপিং এবং জেনেটিক টেস্ট (যেমন - IGH জিন সিন্থেসিস) করার কথা ভাবা হচ্ছে।
২. আইরন সাপ্লিমেন্ট চালিয়ে যাওয়া হচ্ছে।
৩. ৩ সপ্তাহ পর ফলো-আপের জন্য আসতে বলা হয়েছে। কোনো নতুন লক্ষণ দেখা দিলে অবিলম্বে যোগাযোগ করতে হবে।

Doctor: Olá, entre. Sente-se por favor. O que traz hoje? 
Patient: Doctor, tenho uma dor de cabeça e uma protuberância no rosto, do lado direito, acima do olho. A dor já dura cerca de dois meses, e a protuberância também aumentou. Senti miorrexia por um mês. 
Doctor: Entendi. A dor se irradia para a têmpora? 
Patient: Sim, sim. E quando eu mexo o olho, a dor fica muito maior. 
Doctor: Feito. Vou fazer uma ressonância magnética do orbitário, por favor. 
Patient: O que está rolando? Você acha que é algum tumor?

We also need to get a bit more margin from the surrounding healthy tissue since this is on the edge of the lip. We want to make sure all the abnormal cells are gone.

Patient: Okay. And what about the cancer cells? Are they going anywhere else in my system?

Doença de Chédiak-Higashi, mielopatia filmada, neoplasias associadas e outras causas hereditárias de neutropenia foram descartadas com exames complementares. Hemograma com esfregaço de medula óssea normocelular. Itd. Não há achados de deficiência de adesão (CD11b/CD18), deficiência de quimiotaxia (CXCR1/2) ou metástase mieloproliferativa.

A: 1. Doença congênita da função neutrofílica, não especificada. A condição congênita de neutrófilos do paciente apresenta padrão de infecções recorrentes graves sem uma sub-tipologia بواque a बहू दास deficiências específicas de adesão, quimiotaxia, grânulos ou metabolismo oxidativo. A não spesificação atual fundamenta-se na exclusão de síndromes orgânicas ou metabólicas documentadas. 2. Infeção de pele - localizada, tratada. 3. Use contínuo de profilaxia antibiótica.

P: Manter profilaxia com trimetoprima/sulfametoxazol 160/800 mg 3x/dia. Recomendar bronzeamento solar e higiene de rotina. Estudar a possibilidade de HSCT em centro de referência para doença congênita da imunidade primária. Agendar controle trimestral em hematologia. Prescrever antibiótico oral de amplo espectro (amoxicilina/clavulanato) para uso em ritmo/emergência. Evitar corticoides e quimioterapias.

Doctor: Alright, so I have your labs back. What I'm seeing is that your complement levels—your C3 and C4—are really low, basically undetectable on the quantitative assay, and your ANCA panel came back negative. You also mentioned those lesions on your arms and legs, right? The ones that burn and itch. We're looking at a biopsy, and it shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with strong deposition of IgG and C3 along the vessel walls. When you put that together with the low complement and the recurrent urticarial rash, it points to a specific type of immune-complex vasculitis. We call it hypocomplementaemic urticarial vasculitis.

Patient: So am I immune compromised now or something? Are my organs safe?

Doctor: We need to keep a close eye on your kidneys and your lungs, but for now, my goal is to get those rashes under control with hydroxychloroquine and maybe a small dose of prednisone to calm the inflammation. We'll also check your urinalysis and urine protein every month or so to make sure the vasculitis isn't creeping into the kidneys yet.

L'ado 16 ans P.A. MRN:123456789. Dyspnée progressive 3sem, toux sèche, FC 88, TA 110/70, SpO2 94% RA. Rx thorax: strieuses interstitielles bilatérales hileux symétriques, nodules spinaux. PASR 28. Pas de douleur abdominale, pas de céphalées, pas de rash. Sarcoidose pulmonaire probable. Corticoïdes inhaled. Revoir PFT+SACE en 15j.

Doctor: Hello, I am Dr. Patel. I reviewed your labs and symptoms from your last few episodes. Two days before a fevers, your joints swell up and hurt a lot, and your eye gets red and painful. After a day or so, a rash appears on your trunk and limbs, and you feel very tired. The fever goes away after 3 to 5 days without antibiotics, and then you feel normal for a few weeks. You mentioned your uncle had something similar, but Muckle-Wells is not present because you do not have hearing loss or amyloidosis. Family Mediterranean fever is not the right fit either because your pain is mostly in large joints like shoulders and hips, not in your legs or belly. A blood test showed high levels of inflammatory markers, specifically an elevated serum amyloid A and very high C-reactive protein, but your MPO-ANCA and other connective tissue markers were negative. We are going to start you on a biologic called etanercept to block that tumor necrosis factor pathway and stop these flares. Take this prescription; we will follow up in a month to check your response and monitor your side effects.
Patient: Is it serious? Can I still play soccer?
Doctor: With treatment, you should be able to. The goal is to prevent the tissue damage from the chronic inflammation. We will also do an eye exam to make sure the recurrent uveitis is not causing any scarring. Your aunt had this inherited condition, but this particular type is called Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor 1 Associated Periodic Syndrome, which is why it is important to get the exact medication. We will monitor your liver and blood counts while on the new drug.

Doctor: So, we got your results back from the immunology panel. Your C3 levels are borderline low, and your CH50 is coming back as unmeasurable. That basically tells me your early pathway is not firing properly. We're looking at an immunosuppression profile with a deficiency in the early part of that complement cascade, which is why you've been getting these recurrent sinus infections without a clear bacterial cause.

Patient: Oh. So what does that mean? Am I basically just... broken?

Doctor: Not broken, but your immune system is missing a key early warning signal. When the pathogen first enters the bloodstream, the classical pathway should trigger right away, but with the early component missing, the process stalls.

Patient: I tried to look up C3 on the internet. Is that what I have?

Doctor: It's definitely part of the picture. The early pathway relies on C1, C2, and C3 to start the chain reaction. Your history of early-onset sinusitis and the labs together point to a primary immunodeficiency involving that early component.

Patient: And the test for that factor D activity... I saw that on my chart. Is that normal?

Doctor: Yes, that's normal. Factor D is part of the alternative pathway, which is a separate mechanism. The fact that your factor D is fine confirms the problem isn't with the late component or the alternative route. It's specific to the classical initiation.

Patient: I also read about this angioedema thing. Could this cause my throat issues?

Doctor: Angioedema is usually tied to C1 inhibitor problems, either hereditary or acquired. Your levels and the clinical picture just don't fit that pattern at all. I want to reassure you that we ruled that out.

Patient: So what do I do now? Any shots?

Doctor: We'll start by getting you vaccinated against pneumococcus and meningococcus since you lack that early bacterial clearance. I'm going to refer you to a clinical immunology specialist, but I don't think we'll find a late pathway anomaly or any other specified defects when we look at the full panel. The main takeaway today is that we have to treat you as an early component deficiency. We'll monitor your counts regularly and maybe start immunoglobulin replacement if your infections keep worsening despite prophylaxis.

82M. H. Pt. ref: ataxia, crisis simp. Examen físico y laboratorios. Diagnóstico: Trastornos del metabolismo de aminas biógenas, no especificado. Plan: suspender IECA. Rx antihistamínico. Seguir en 15 días.

Doctor: வணக்கம், என்ன பிரச்சனை? சோர்வா இருக்கீங்களா? Patient: ஆமாம் சார், காய்ச்சல், இரவு வியர்வை, எடை குறைவு, மூட்டு வலி, மற்றும் தோலில் பெரிய அரிப்பு. அதுமட்டுமின்றி, என் வயிறு மற்றும் வாய் முழுவதும் புண்கள் உள்ளன. Doctor: இவை அனைத்தும் உங்கள் உடலில் உள்ள இரத்த செல்கள் மற்றும் காய்ச்சல் பிரச்சனையின் அறிகுறிகளாக இருக்கலாம். இது ஒரு மிகைவான நோயெதிர்ப்பு எதிர்வினையால் ஏற்படும் பிரைமரி ஹீமோபாகோசைடிக் லிம்போஹிஸ்டியோசைடோசிஸ், அதாவது HLH-க்கான அறிகுறியாக இருக்கலாம். நாம் இதைச் சரியாகப் பரிசோதனை செய்ய வேண்டும். Patient: நோக்கம் என்ன டாக்டர்? Doctor: நாம் இதை முழுமையாகச் சரிபார்க்க வேண்டும். உங்கள் கல்லீரல் மற்றும் மண்ணீரலின் செயல்பாடுகள், மற்றும் பிற உறுப்புகளின் நிலையை அறிய சில பரிசோதனைகள் செய்ய வேண்டியிருக்கும். Doctor: Hey Jenny, thanks for coming in. I wanted to follow up on that chronic GVHD we discussed after your second transplant. Patient: Yes, I’m still having trouble swallowing. Everything feels tight and I’m drooling a bit. Doctor: That fits with the chronic GVHD involving your mouth and esophagus. You mentioned some skin tightening on your hands too? Patient: Right, my hands feel like they’re shrinking. My fingers are stiff and I can’t open them all the way. Doctor: So we’re looking at chronic GVHD affecting your oral mucosa, the esophagus, and your skin. Have you noticed any fevers, night sweats, or rashes that come on suddenly? Patient: No, nothing like that. It’s all been gradual over the past eight months. Doctor: Good. That helps rule out the acute form. We don’t want to confuse chronic with something acute. Patient: Okay. So what’s the plan? Doctor: I’m going to increase your prednisone to 1 mg per kilo and add some tacrolimus. We’ll also start you on a new mouth rinse and a bland diet to protect your esophagus. We’ll see you back in four weeks to check your skin mobility and swallow. For now, avoid spicy foods and keep using the artificial tears we prescribed. Does that sound okay? Patient: Yes, that sounds fine. Thank you.

Doctor: Alright, I'm going to order some metabolic screening and liver function tests, as well as a basic thyroid panel to rule out common causes of fatigue. I want to evaluate your overall metabolic baseline and make sure we aren't missing something else.

Doctor: So what brings you in today, little one? Patient: My tummy hurts, doctor. I've been throwing up a lot, and I've had to pee all the time. Doctor: So tell me, what brings you in today? Patient: I've just been feeling really weak and tired lately. I get this burning in my mouth and my tongue looks kind of pale and sore. Doctor: I see. I just take a multivitamin sometimes, but lately I haven't because I keep forgetting. Doctor: Okay, from your symptoms and the tiredness, I'm concerned you might have a deficiency. I'll run some blood work to check your vitamin levels and hemoglobin. The fatigue, the sore mouth, and the tingling points toward a specific nutritional deficiency, likely due to your poor diet. If the blood work confirms low levels, we'll start you on a folate supplement and get you on a better diet. For now, avoid alcohol since that can mess with absorption.

S:  62M presents with a 3-month history of progressive peripheral vision loss and inability to see clearly in dim lighting. He has a chronic history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and malnutrition, with poor dietary intake of fruits and vegetables over the last 5 years. The patient reports difficulty navigating the house at night and has fallen twice recently due to vision impairment. He denies any eye pain or redness. He is a former smoker with 40 pack-years. 

O:  Vitals stable. Ophthalmic exam: Right eye shows extensive, dense, bilateral corneal opacification and scarring involving the central visual axis. Left eye shows similar scarring extending to the visual axis. Pupils are sluggish to direct light but brisk to consensual. Extraocular movements are full and non-painful. Anterior chamber is deep and quiet. Fundoscopy reveals mild optic disc pallor. Visual acuity is counting fingers at 3 feet in both eyes. 

Blepharospasm and lagophthalmos are absent. Schirmer's test is negative. There is no evidence of acute corneal ulceration or melting. 

A:  1. Vitamin A deficiency with xerophthalmic scars of cornea and blindness (bilateral). 
   2. COPD exacerbation in remission. 

P:  1. Prescribe high-dose oral Vitamin A (200,000 IU) daily for 5 days as per WHO protocol, followed by monthly maintenance (100,000 IU) for 3 months. 
   2. Order baseline serum retinol level and liver function tests. 
   3. Refer to ophthalmology for detailed macular imaging and low-vision rehabilitation; counsel on the permanent nature of the corneal scarring and potential for blindness. 
   4. Optimize COPD regimen and provide nutritional counseling focusing on dietary supplementation (retinol-rich foods, fortified foods). 

Discussions: Patient was counseled on the irreversible nature of his corneal scarring. Compliance with vitamin A supplementation was emphasized. Follow-up in 1 week for toxicity monitoring.

Doctor: नमस्कार. तुमचे रक्त तपासणीचे रिपोर्ट आले आहेत. मला सांगायला आनंद होतोय की तुमचे हायपरथायरॉयडिझमचे उपचार आता बऱ्यापैकी यशस्वी होत आहेत. गेल्या महिन्याच्या तपासणीत तुम्हाला थायरॉईडचा त्रास होता, जो आता नियंत्रणात आला आहे. तुमच्या मानेवर आता कोणताही मोठा सूज किंवा ग्रंथी दिसत नाही, आणि तुमचे वजन आणि हृदयाचे ठोके आता स्थिर आहेत. त्यामुळे आम्ही तुमची औषधे थोड्या प्रमाणात कमी करणार आहोत. पुढच्या महिन्यात पुन्हा रक्त तपासणी करू. काही त्रास वाटल्यास मला नक्की संपर्क करा. S: Masculino, 31 anos, solicitou avaliação urinária por histórica de cálculos renais bilaterais e dor lombar episódica. Relataoksiuria e polidipsia noturna há 2 anos. Familiarmente, pai e irmão tiveram cálculos renais na juventude. Não há história de glaucoma, distrofia muscular ou acidose tubular renal. Consumo de vitamina C ~1g/dia em automedicação.

O: Exame físico sem alteração. Laboratório: ácido úrico 4.2 mg/dL (normo), creatinina sérica 0.9 mg/dL, pH urinário 7.5-8.0 (alada), nitrito e leucócitos negativos, proteinúria <50 mg/24h, urina com mau odor e pH alcalino. Dosagem urinária: cysteína 480 mg/24h (aumentada), arginina 45 mg/24h (normo), lisina 38 mg/24h (normo), ornitina 12 mg/24h (normo). Hemograma e VHS normais. Ultrassonografia renal bilateral: duas sementes renais bilaterais bilaterais de 4 mm (RKI) e 6 mm (RKI), sem hidronefrose. Aterosclerose grade III bilateral.

A: Diagnóstico de Cistinúria (distúrbio do transporte renal de aminoácidos dibásicos/cisteína), tipo hereditário, que explica a acidose tubular renal distal? sem manifestações extra renais, calculopatia renais (nefrolitíase por cysteína), com nefigopatia incipiente (A1a). Differential: se excluiu cistinose (sem fotofobia, falangeopatia, distrofia muscular, ou acidose tubular proximal) e sévica síndrome de Clarke-Gullaine (sem glaucoma e acidose tubular distal). Não há evidências de tubulose intersticial renal autoinflamatório.

P: 1. Hidratação agresiva — >3 L/dia de água pura, com alcalinização da urina (NaHCO3 1-1.5 g/dia em 3 doses). 2. Colestiramina 4g/dia como surfactante de cysteína (inibidor da cristalização), dividida em 2 doses. 3. Aprofundar exames genéticos para mutação SLC3A1 / SLC7A9, conforme orientações. 4. Neuromodulador de dor lombar intermitente PRN. 5. Repassar doente na clínica de nefrologia em 6 semanas. 6. Actualizar fichário de prescrição com nomes dos medicamentos: D-penicilamina e tiopronina, para uso futuro se a profilaxia farmacológica não for suficiente. 7. Actualizar anamnese familiar para glaucoma. 8. Realizar mesa-redonda com a equipe de nefrologia sobre a condição de "disorder of amino acid absorption or transport" hereditário, com recomendação de monitorização da função renal e da densidade mineral óssea.

S: 14-year-old male presents with 3-week history of progressive malaise, nausea, polyuria, and diffuse muscle aches. No visual disturbances. Denies recent liver toxicity or high-dose retinoid use. Symptoms began after starting a new herbal supplement recommended by a gym trainer for 'immune support' and 'bone health' (unlabeled). No family history of inherited hypercalcemia syndromes. No known comorbid conditions.

O: Vitals stable. IVC flat; no peripheral edema. Extremities soft. No rash, no lymphadenopathy. No hepatosplenomegaly. No neuro-ophthalmic deficits to suggest toxic optic neuropathy.

Labs: Ca 15.8 mg/dL (high), ionized Ca 7.2 mmol/L, PO4 low-normal. PTH suppressed to <5 pg/mL. 25-OH vitamin D level 243 ng/mL (markedly elevated). 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D mildly elevated. Serum retinol and liver function tests normal. Urine Ca/Cr clearance ratio normal. EKG shows QT shortening.

A: 1. Vitamin D toxicity (hypervitaminosis D) secondary to chronic overuse of an unlabeled herbal/nutriceutical supplement.

2. Secondary hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria with nephrocalcinosis risk, to be monitored with serial U/S and ABGs if symptomatic.

P: 1. Immediate cessation of the supplement.
2. PO fluids and loop diuretics to lower serum calcium and promote calciuresis.
3. Refer to pediatric endocrinology for follow-up bone density monitoring and 24-hour urine calcium studies.
4. Avoid dairy and calcium supplements until levels normalize.
5. Return to ED or call if worsening vomiting, confusion, or altered mental status.

S: पेशंट 38 वर्षीय स्त्री आहे. 4 महिन्यांपूर्वी ती एका NGO च्या पुनर्वसन केंद्रातून परत आली आहे. तिथे गेल्या 6 महिन्यांपासून तिला अन्नाची तीव्र टंचाई होती. घरी आल्यापासून भूक नसणे, सुस्ती, केस गळणे आणि स्नायूंमध्ये अशक्तपणा असा त्रास ती सांगत आहे. आहाराची सवय सुधारली असली तरी, या समस्यांमध्ये कोणतीही सुधारणा झालेली नाही.

O: तपासणी केली असता, BMI 17.2 kg/m² आहे. दोन्ही टेंडन्सचे डीप टेंडन रिफ्लेक्सेस कमी झाले आहेत (बायसेप्स आणि अकिलीस). तिला चालताना अस्थिरता जाणवते. हाता-पायावर 'Flaky paint' सारखे त्वचेचे पापुद्रे दिसतात. सामान्य अशक्तपणा आहे. CBC आणि इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स नॉर्मल आहेत. इतर कोणतीही तीव्र आजारनिदानाचा संबंध नाही.

A: जुनाट कुपोषणाचे परिणाम. (अनिर्दिष्ट उपप्रकार).

P: 1. तिची आहाराची सवय सुधारण्यासाठी आणि कॅलरीचे प्रमाण वाढवण्यासाठी आहारतज्ज्ञाकडे पाठवणे.
2. स्नायूंची पुनर्बांधणी आणि सामान्य अशक्तपणासाठी फिजिओथेरपी सुरू करणे.
3. व्हिटॅमिन B कॉम्प्लेक्स आणि लोह (Iron) च्या गोळ्या सुरू करणे.
4. 4 आठवड्यांनी पुनरावलोकन (Follow-up).

Pt 16m hoy por consulta PP. Dice que no usa nada desde hace 4 meses; último uso de marihuana/shisha fue 1/9. No antojo, ya no va a fiestas. AA/NA positivo, sin síntomas de abstinencia. Plan: continuar seguimiento ambulatorio cada 3 meses, sin necesidad de PCR. No hay comorbilidades.

S: Paciente do sexo masculino (M), 14 anos, assistido em consultório por pai. Reclama de sofrimento emocional, irritabilidade e dificuldades de concentração nas últimas 6 semanas. Relata que o filho se ausentou da escola e mentiu sobre o motivo. O pai relata que o paciente tem passado grandes quantias de dinheiro e que o banco local avisou sobre movimentações suspeitas nas contas correntes do adolescente. O paciente relata que se sente incapaz de deixar de jogar (loteria e jogos de azar) e que tentou parar por si só, sem sucesso. O paciente afirma que seus amigos jogam muito, e que a preoccupation com a jogatina interfere com suas atividades diárias e com a interação familiar. A mãe informa que o paciente tem um histórico de TDAH diagnosticado na infância, que está em uso de Ritalina de liberação prolongada. Não há uso de substâncias, tabaco ou álcool.

O: Acompanhamento do adolescente. A motorique e a linguagem estão normais para idade. Estado de humor deprimido, com afetação emocional instável. No teste de mini-mental (adapted), o paciente apresenta distúrbio de atenção e impulsividade. O sistema cardiovascular, neurológico e abdominal estão normais.

Dx: Transtorno do jogo, não especificado. [Outros: TDAH; TDAH, combinado].

P: Continue o Ritalina 40mg/dia (liberação prolongada) para o TDAH. Acompanhamento programado em 4 semanas com psiquiatria infantil. Recomenda-se acompanhamento psicoterapêutico (TCC) focada em comportamentos compulsivos. Explicado ao paciente e ao pai sobre o diagnóstico de transtorno do jogo. O adolescente concordou com o acompanhamento, mas nega necessidade de internação psiquiátrica. A equipe de saúde mental será incluída para avaliação e acompanhamento contínuo. Repassar orientações sobre limites de acesso a dinheiro e a internet.

Doctor: I’m reviewing your chart and wanted to check in on your substance use. I see you’ve been vaping and smoking almost every day since school started. Do you feel like you’re able to cut back or stop, or does it feel like something you can’t really control? I’m asking because from what I’m seeing, it sounds like the nicotine use is causing problems for you—like missing class, getting into fights with your parents, or staying up all night because you can’t sleep without having a cigarette. In medical terms, we call this a harmful pattern of nicotine use. The key thing is that it’s not fitting a clean episodic or continuous mold right now; it’s more irregular, but clearly damaging to your health and daily life. We’re going to focus on trying to quit and getting you connected to a counselor who can help you manage the cravings. We’ll also run a quick urine test to confirm your baseline nicotine levels and rule out any other substances. Does that make sense to you? Do you have any questions at all? 
Patient: Yeah, actually, I was wondering if cutting down to just a few puffs a day would be okay instead of quitting cold turkey. I get really shaky and angry if I don’t have one. 
Doctor: I understand that feeling, but the goal here is total cessation. Even just a few puffs per day keeps the addiction going and still exposes your lungs to harmful chemicals. I’m going to write a prescription for a nicotine patch to help with withdrawal, and I want to see you back in two weeks. In the meantime, if you feel overwhelming cravings, you can try the 4-7-8 breathing technique we discussed. 
Patient: Okay, I’ll try. Thanks. 
Doctor: You’re welcome. Keep up with your inhaler for your asthma, and let me know if you develop any chest pain before we meet again.

Doctor: नमस्कार, इथे आलंय. आज काय झालंय ते सांगा. Patient: काल रात्री मित्रासोबत पार्टीत गेलो होतो. तिथे कोणीतरी मला ती पावडर दिली. Doctor: कोणती पावडर? Patient: ती निळ्या रंगाची, मॅजिक किंवा मॉली म्हणतात ती. मी ती थोडी घेतली, म्हणून पोटात खूप कळा आल्या आणि खूप घाम आला. Doctor: तेव्हापासून काही त्रास होतोय का? Patient: हो, डोक्यात खूप गोंधळ उडालाय. काल रात्रीपासून नीट झोप लागलेली नाही. आणि आता वाटतंय की कोणीतरी माझ्या मागे आहे, भिंतीतले लोक हलतातय. Doctor: तुम्ही आता कोठे आहात? Patient: मी रूमवर आहे, पण मला बाहेर जायचंच नाहीये, वाटतंय कोणीतरी मला पकडेल. डॉक्टर: तुमचे डोळे कसे आहेत? Patient: खूप लाल झालेत. हृदयाचे ठोके पण खूप जोरात चालू आहेत. डॉक्टर: मी सगळं नीट ऐकलंय. तुम्ही पार्टीत जी निळी पावडर घेतली, ती 'बाथ सॉल्ट्स' होती. त्यामुळे तुमच्या मेंदूवर परिणाम झाला आहे. आता तुम्हाला जो गोंधळ उडालाय आणि भिंतीत लोक दिसतायत, हा 'सिंथेटिक काथिनोनमुळे झालेला गोंधळ' आहे. तुम्हाला इथेच राहून शांत राहणं आणि थोडा आराम करणं खूप गरजेचं आहे. डॉक्टर: आता तुम्ही इथेच थांबा आणि नीट श्वास घ्या. आम्ही तुम्हाला काही औषधं देतोय, जेणेकरून तुम्हाला झोप येईल आणि तुमचा गोंधळ कमी होईल. लवकरच तुम्हाला बरं वाटेल.
Pt 42y M c/o 6mo hx depressed, anhedonic, insomnia x3wks. Screener 21/27. No hx mania/hypo. No psychosis. Started fluoxetine 20mg qd. PCP follow-up.

S: ২৮ বছর বয়সী সিঙ্গল ফিমেল, যিনি গত ৬ মাস ধরে মানসিক অস্থিরতা এবং মেজাজের চরম পরিবর্তন নিয়ে উপস্থিত হয়েছেন। রোগী জানিয়েছেন যে তার কোনো স্পষ্ট সাইকোটিক লক্ষণ নেই এবং তার চিন্তাভাবনা স্বাভাবিক। লেবার ডে-তে তার আইনি সমস্যা ছিল, তবে তিনি এখন তা অস্বীকার করছেন। কোনো হ্যালুসিনেশন বা ডিলিউশনের কথা বিশেষভাবে অস্বীকার করেছেন। ক্রনিক পিটিএসডি-এর পূর্ব ইতিহাস রয়েছে। বর্তমানে কোনো অ্যাকিউট মেডিকেশন অ্যাডহেরেন্সের অভাব নেই।

O: ভিটালস: বিপি ১০৫/৭০, এইচআর ৬২, টিপি ৯৮.৮° এফ, আরআর ১৬, ও২ স্যাচ ৮৯% রুম এয়ারে। মুড: অ্যাফেক্ট ফ্ল্যাট, সীমাবদ্ধ। চিন্তাভাবনা: লজিক্যাল। ইনসাইট: সীমিত। জাজমেন্ট: অক্ষত। সি অ্যান্ড এইচ-এ কোনো দৃশ্যমান ব্যথার লক্ষণ নেই।

A: সিজোঅ্যাফেক্টিভ ডিসঅর্ডার, আনস্পেসিফাইড। সিজার বা মাইগ্রেনের কোনো সিঙ্ক্রোনাইজড ইতিহাস নেই। টিসিএ (TCA) অ্যান্টিডিপ্রেসেন্ট দিয়ে ট্রামাডোল শুরু করা হয়েছে। মানসিক স্থিতিশীলতা নিশ্চিত করতে ফলো-আপ শিডিউল করা হয়েছে।

P: ১. সিজোঅ্যাফেক্টিভ, আনস্পেসিফাইড।
২. পিটিএসডি (PTSD)।
৩. মানসিক কাউন্সেলিং এবং কগনিটিভ বিহেভিওরাল থেরাপির রেফারেল দেওয়া হয়েছে।
৪. আগামী ২ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে সাইকিয়াট্রিস্টের সাথে ফলো-আপ অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট।

Doctor: আপনার কী মনে হচ্ছে, কেন আজকে এখানে এলেন? Patient: আসলে রাতে খুব মাথা ঘুরছিল, বমি বমি লাগছিল, আর চোখে কিছু দেখতে সমস্যা হচ্ছিল। Doctor: আচ্ছা, আপনি কি কোনো ওষুধ খেয়েছেন? Patient: হ্যাঁ, সত্যিই বলতে গেলে কাল রাতে আমি একটু বেশিই খেয়ে ফেলেছিলাম। আমার এক বন্ধু আমাকে কিছু নীল রঙের পিল আর একটা সাদা পাউডার দিয়েছিল ঘুমের জন্য। আমি সে দুটোই খেয়ে নিয়েছিলাম। Doctor: তাহলে আপনি দুটোই নিয়েছিলেন। আপনি কোনোটা খাওয়া শুরু করার আগে, আপনার কি কোনো শারীরিক বা মানসিক সমস্যা আছে? Patient: না, আগে থেকেই আমার কোনো সমস্যা নেই। Doctor: আচ্ছা, আপনার রক্তচাপ আর হার্ট রেট একটু বেশি আছে, আর আপনি একটু অস্থির বোধ করছেন। আমি একটা ইসিজি (ECG) আর ব্লাড টেস্ট করে নেব। আপনি সারারাত ওষুধগুলো খেয়েছেন, তাই এটাই 'ড্রাগ ইনটক্সিকেশন' বা নেশার প্রভাব, কিন্তু আপনার ডোপামিন রিসেপ্টরগুলো এখন ওভারস্টিমুলেটেড আছে। আমাদের শুধু Supportive care দিতে হবে, হালকা ঘুমের ওষুধ আর হাইড্রেশন। আপনার যদি আবার এমন সমস্যা হয়, তবে সাথে সাথে ইমার্জেন্সিতে আসবেন। Patient: ঠিক আছে, আমি ওষুধগুলো আর খাব না।

Doctor: Good morning. I’m glad you could make it in today.
Patient: Morning, doc. I don’t know, I just haven’t been myself lately, you know? My wife passed about seven months ago and I’m still not over it, I think.
Doctor: I can imagine how hard that has been. Tell me what you’re feeling right now.
Patient: It’s just like a weight on my chest all the time. I don’t care about my woodcarving anymore, and I used to love that. Food just tastes like cardboard. I wake up around 4 a.m. every morning and I can’t get back to sleep. I feel guilty, like I’m failing my kids because I can’t get out of bed to take them to school. I feel slow, like my brain is in mud. I’ve even thought, you know, maybe it’s better if I just wasn’t here.
Doctor: That sounds incredibly heavy. When did this start, or did it get worse after the loss?
Patient: It was okay for a bit, but around month four it really crashed. I’ve been like this for about three months now, doc. I see my oldest every other weekend, but I can’t really talk to them, I just feel empty.
Doctor: I hear that. The sleep changes, the loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, the guilt, and the trouble concentrating—these are all classic signs of a persistent depression, especially since we’re now well past the initial grief reaction. Have you had any panic attacks, like heart racing out of nowhere? Or are your symptoms mainly low mood and anhedonia?
Patient: No, no panic attacks. Just the sadness and the hopelessness.
Doctor: Any seasonal pattern to when this gets bad?
Patient: Not really. It’s just been steady since I lost my wife.
Doctor: No racing thoughts, no grandiosity, or energy spikes?
Patient: No, I’m just tired all the time.
Doctor: And no vegetative signs of melancholia—you don’t feel worse in the morning, and your weight hasn’t dropped significantly, have you?
Patient: I actually snack more late at night, but I’m not sleeping through the night anyway. I feel depressed, but not like a blank slate or anything weird.
Doctor: So, to summarize, it sounds like you’re dealing with a prolonged depressive episode. It’s not just grief, and it’s not episodic with panic or seasonal drops. It’s just been a steady low mood for months now. We should start talking about treatment. I’m thinking of a low-dose SSRI and maybe some structured therapy for the grief and the depression. Does that sound okay to you?
Patient: Yeah, whatever helps. I’m just tired of feeling this way.
Doctor: We’ll start you on the medication this week and get you set up with therapy. I’ll see you back in two weeks to check in.

S: Paciente varón de 62 años refiere ronquidos nocturnos no perturbadores, somnolencia diurna leve desde hace 3 meses. No refiere cefaleas matutinas ni pausas respiratorias observadas por cónyuge. Niega uso de opioides, CPAP ni otros aparatos respiratorios. El paciente refiere episodio de neumonía hace 8 meses, pero ya está recuperado. No refiere acropaquia.

O: Examen físico sin hallazgos significativos. SAT 98% en sala. Tonometría intraocular dentro de lo normal.

A: Ronquidos e hipopneas obstructivas leves. En base a polisomnografía ambulatoria, hallazgos compatibles con apnea central durante el sueño. No se observa patrón de Cheyne-Stokes. No se identifica causa subyacente específica ni uso de neurolépticos que explique el evento.

P: Diagnóstico: Apneas centrales del sueño, no especificado. Se le indica al paciente realizar un estudio de sueño polisomnográfico nocturno formal para confirmar la clasificación. Se le receta Rivotril 0.25 mg nocturno temporalmente para estabilizar el patrón respiratorio. Se reevaluará en 6 semanas.

S: Patient avec antécédents de développement intellectuel global modéré-léger. Aîné d'une fratrie de 3 enfants. Motricité marche précoce, langage phrases simples à 4 ans. Scolarité en ULIS jusqu'à 16 ans, avec soutien orthophonique et psychomotricité. Autonomie relative en ADL, mais difficulté avec la planification et la résolution de problèmes abstraits. Contexte familial stable. Pas de retard moteur significatif. Évolution stable sous accompagnement spécifique (IPP/UPE2D).

O: Bilan neuropsychologique de 2024: QIC estimé de 55-60, à la limite du QI faible sans atteindre le retard mental modéré. Compétences langagières: compréhension orale correcte, expression limitée avec un vocabulaire de 5 ans et des phrases syntaxiquement simples et brèves. Fonctions exécutives déficitaires, particulièrement en organisation et en flexibilité cognitive. Tests de mémoire épisodique et de raisonnement verbal: scores dans le bas de la moyenne. Pas de dyspraxie majeure, pas de troubles des apprentissages spécifiques (dyslexie, dyscalculie) en dessous de 5 ans. Pas de troubles psychotiques, pas d'épisodes dépressifs majeurs. Examen neurologique: une légère hypertonicité des membres inférieurs de type spastique, sans signe pyramidal central. Pas de crises cliniques.

A: 1) Trouble du développement intellectuel, léger (F71). Diagnostic de 1ère consultation confirmé. 2) Spasticité mineure des membres inférieurs (G21.4).

P: Continue de l'IPP/UPE2D. Recommandation d'un suivi neuropsychologique et psychologique pour renforcer les compensations. Maintenir le suivi en ORL pour surveiller l'audition. Avis de transport: continuer de se déplacer seul pour les occupations proches, éviter les situations à forte complexité spatiale sans aide.

रुग्ण: F/28, MS. MS झटकेवर स्थिर. आजच्या भेटीत: दिवसा खूप जास्त झोप येते, झोपेत अचानक स्नायू कमकुवत होऊन खाली पडल्यासारखे वाटते (cataplexy-सारखी episodes, पण नक्की नाही), आणि रात्री चांगली झोप होऊनही ताजेतवाने वाटत नाही. polysomnography negative, MS relapse negative. Plan: Sodium oxybate सुरू करणे आणि झोपेच्या स्वच्छतेचा सल्ला (sleep hygiene advice).}

Doctor: So, tell me what's been keeping you up at night lately, or in your case, keeping you asleep during the day when you need to be alert. Patient: It's just the schedule. I work the overnight shift at the warehouse. I'm on from 10 PM to 6 AM. I sleep during the day and then I wake up around 4 AM and can't get back to sleep. By the time I get to my sleep at 9 PM, I'm just wide awake and my mind is racing because the body clock is fighting the shift. Doctor: I see. When did this start? Patient: It started about two months ago when they changed the rotation. Before that, I was on a rotating schedule, but now I'm stuck in nights permanently. Doctor: Have you tried any sleep hygiene or dark curtains? Patient: I wear an eye mask and earplugs. It helps a little, but I'm still tired when I start my shift. Doctor: It sounds like you're having trouble staying asleep during the day and adjusting your body clock to the night schedule. This is consistent with a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder due to shift work. We'll skip the sleep study and focus on adjusting your light exposure and shift scheduling strategies. We'll also avoid any long-acting sedatives that might make you groggy at work. How does that sound?

S: 17 y/o M presents for outpatient sleep evaluation. Pt reports recurring episodes of vivid dream-enactment and daytime sleep paralysis over the past 6 months, occurring several times per week. Episodes involve shouting, arm flailing, and attempts to punch. He does not recall these events upon awakening. He also reports occasional terrifying dreams that awaken him from REM sleep, but does not meet full criteria. No nocturnal wandering or complex sleep-related eating. Denies cataplexy, hypnagogic hallucinations, and excessive daytime sleepiness. No prior nocturnal motor episodes per bed partner. No syncopal events. No history of CNS infection, trauma, or medication changes.

O: Vitals: BP 118/74, HR 68, SpO2 99% RA.

Exam: Neurologic: Alert, oriented x4, cranial nerves II-XII intact. Motor and sensation intact. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

He was awake and interactive. Repeating 4-week sleep log provided. PSG review: Sleep onset latency normal, sleep architecture preserved, REM latency 95 min. REM suppression noted with minimal limb movements (PLMs < 8/hr). No frank REM without atonia or actigraphy-documented complex behaviors. No episodes of prolonged REM with vocalizations captured. EEG during episodes shows normal REM patterns without epileptiform activity.

A: REM sleep-related parasomnia, unspecified.

P: 1) Avoid sleep deprivation and alcohol; implement standard sleep hygiene.
2) Continue follow-up in 4 weeks; consider initiation of melatonin 5 mg nightly if nocturnal episodes persist.
3) Screen for underlying obstructive sleep apnea/hypopnea syndrome at next visit.
4) Avoid medications that suppress REM sleep (e.g., SSRIs) or trigger REM atonia loss if possible.
5) Avoid REM-suppressing agents. Refer to neurology for video-PSG if episodes escalate.

S: 68 y/o male presents to sleep clinic for evaluation of sleep-related movements. Reports 8-month history of vivid, often violent dream enactment. Patient's wife describes episodes of yelling, punching, and jumping out of bed during sleep. Events typically occur 3-4 times per week, lasting up to 5 minutes. Patient reports no recall of dreams or actions. No history of sleep paralysis. No nightmares reported. No daytime sleepiness. Past medical history: hypertension, depression. No relevant family history for sleep disorders, dementia, or movement disorders.

O: Vitals: BP 130/82, HR 72, BMI 27. Neurological exam findings are within normal limits. No evidence of parkinsonism (bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, postural instability). Doctor: Welcome, I’m Dr. Taylor. I’m here to talk about your sleep schedule and how school is affecting you.

Doctor: That’s pretty common in your age group, but your sleep timing looks shifted way later than the clock. I think you have what we call a Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder, basically a delayed circadian rhythm. Does that make sense?

Doctor: So, I've been looking over your sleep logs and the actigraphy data from the monitor you wore for the past two weeks. Patient: Yeah, I wore it all the time, even when I was working the night shift. I tried, Doc. I really tried. Doctor: I see that. It says you were in bed for about nine to ten hours a night, yet your sleep efficiency is only around 82 percent. Patient: So I was only asleep for eight hours? But I feel like I was sleeping the whole time. Doctor: Exactly. The data shows you slept for roughly 640 minutes. But you also had about 120 minutes of wake time after sleep onset. Patient: That sounds right. I'd wake up, hit the snooze button, and just drift right back off. I'm still exhausted when the alarm goes off at 6 AM. Doctor: And when you do finally get up, how does that grogginess feel? Patient: Like I'm walking through mud. It takes me an hour, sometimes two, to feel human enough to drive to work. And once I'm there, I have these naps. I'll just sit at my desk and my head will drop. I know I shouldn't, but I can't help it. I had to pull over on the highway yesterday because my eyes wouldn't stay open. Doctor: I can see why. Your Epworth Sleepiness Scale score was 18, which puts you in the severe range. I also wanted to rule out a few things. You mentioned that you don't have any major joint pain or morning stiffness, and your wife says you don't snore or gasp much, right? Patient: No, I don't snore. And my joints feel fine. Just tired. Doctor: Good. We ran a sleep study last year, and it came back clean. No sleep apnea, no narcolepsy. You don't have hypothyroidism, your ferritin is normal, and your thyroid panel is completely within range. Patient: So I haven't been giving myself enough time? I've been trying to sleep eight hours a night. Doctor: Eight hours of time in bed isn't the same as eight hours of actual sleep, and your total sleep time is definitely below the threshold for hypersomnia. After reviewing everything and ruling out all the secondary causes—like sleep apnea, narcolepsy, and thyroid issues—I can give you the formal diagnosis. You have a primary sleep disorder called idiopathic hypersomnia. Patient: Just... sleepiness? For no reason? Doctor: Yes. It's not a problem with your sleep architecture or your body clock; it's a problem with your sleep drive and your ability to wake up. We'll start you on a wake-promoting medication, like modafinil, and I want to refer you to a psychologist to help you manage the cognitive load and your anxiety about safety at work. We'll follow up in six weeks to see how the medication is affecting your daytime alertness and your office naps.

Doctor: Good morning, come in and have a seat. What brings you in today?
Patient: I'm here for the follow-up on the headache and the eye stuff. It’s been getting worse since the last visit.
Doctor: How long exactly have you been getting these head pains?
Patient: About two months now. They started as a dull ache behind the eyes, mostly in the mornings. Lately they're getting sharp and throbbing, and I've been vomiting in the mornings too. My vision sometimes gets blurry and I've been seeing spots.
Doctor: Have you been taking any new supplements or vitamins at home?
Patient: Yeah, my mom got me this high-dose Vitamin A supplement from the internet. She said it's for my eyes. I've been taking it every morning for three weeks.
Doctor: Can you tell me exactly what it is and how much you're taking?
Patient: It's a mega-dose Vitamin A capsule, 25,000 IU. I take one every day. I've been using it for acne too.
Doctor: I'm going to do a quick neurological exam right now. [checking reflexes] Your reflexes are fine. [checking vision] Do you have any problem seeing things in your side vision?
Patient: Yes, I keep bumping into things on my left side.
Doctor: Are you having any muscle weakness or tingling in your hands or feet?
Patient: No, my hands and feet feel fine. No tingling at all.
Doctor: Have you had any recent issues with your calcium levels or muscle pain?
Patient: No, my calcium was normal in my last blood work. No muscle pain.
Doctor: Based on your symptoms of morning headaches, vomiting, blurred vision, blind spots, and papilledema, along with your heavy Vitamin A use, this sounds like Pseudotumour Cerebri caused by too much Vitamin A.
Patient: So it's a tumour?
Doctor: It is not a real tumour. It is a condition where there is increased pressure inside the skull that looks like a tumour on imaging, but it is caused by the excess Vitamin A. We need to stop the supplement immediately and start treatment to lower the eye pressure.
Patient: Okay. I will stop taking it today.
Doctor: We will start you on acetazolamide to help with the fluid buildup and refer you to ophthalmology for regular visual field testing. Make sure you do not take any more of that supplement. We will see you back in two weeks.

36-year-old female presents with sudden-onset left-sided hemiparesis and expressive aphasia. Symptoms began 3 hours prior to arrival. She denies headache, neck pain, or recent trauma. No facial droop reported. Home medications: none. Past medical history: migraine with aura, no known cardiac disease. Social history: ex-smoker, 5 pack-year history, stopped 2 years ago. No family history of clotting disorders. No recent infections, prolonged immobilization, or hormonal contraceptive use.

O:
BP: 148/88 mmHg. HR: 82 bpm, regular. Afebrile. Neurological exam: 4/5 strength in left arm and leg, left-sided facial droop, fluent aphasia with impaired repetition, right visual field cut. NIHSS: 9. CT head (non-contrast): no acute intracranial hemorrhage; small territorial infarct in the right MCA distribution. CTA of head and neck: no large vessel occlusion. MRI brain with DWI: acute infarct in the right parietal lobe (M2 branch territory). MRA of intracranial vessels: focal irregular stenosis of the right distal MCA with adjacent vessel wall thickening and enhancement consistent with vasculitis. No cervical arterial dissection. No evidence of global hypoperfusion or bilateral watershed infarcts. Blood work: normal CBC, CMP, coagulation panel, no hypercoagulable panel ordered. No signs of subarachnoid hemorrhage.

A:
1. Acute cerebral ischemic stroke due to other non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy (inflammatory/vasculitic).
2. Migraine with aura - Hx.

P:
1. Admission to stroke unit for IV thrombolysis evaluation (within window, no contraindications).
2. Start aspirin 81 mg daily (unless thrombolyzed then hold per protocol).
3. High-dose IV methylprednisolone 1g daily for 3-5 days for presumed autoimmune cerebral vasculitis; neurology and rheumatology to evaluate for secondary causes.
4. PFTs and chest imaging to rule out other systemic vasculitides before long-term immunosuppression.
5. Monitor neuro status q1h; swallow evaluation prior to oral intake.
6. Continue cardiology/echocardiogram workup to exclude cardioembolic source.

Doctor: Olá, entre, sente-se. Como você tem passado ultimamente?
Patient: Bom dia, doutor. Andando. Tenho 14 anos. As minhas mãos começaram a tremer quando eu vou pegar o mouse na escola ou scrivere em casa. As minhas notas ficaram péssimas. Ninguém sabe o que é, o meu pai também não tem coisa nestas coisas, acho que é preciso de stress.
Doctor: Entendo. Por quanto tempo tem percebido esse tremor?
Patient: Há cerca de dois meses. É pior quando eu tenho uma prova ou estou preocupado. A gente diz que é nervoso, mas o que eu quero saber é se não é algo grave, tipo paralisia cerebral ou alguma coisa assim que eleta?
Doctor: Vamos ver. Na última consulta pedi um exame de ressonância magnética do cérebro por فنی. O resultado veio normal. O tremore só aparece quando você está tentando fazer uma tarefa precisa, como escrever ou usar o computador, e é bilateral, sim?
Patient: Sim, nos dois lados. Nem sempre, só quando preciso de precisionar.
Doctor: E por acaso você já tomou ou tomou algum tipo de medicação que possa causar isso? Algum remédio para a alergia, por exemplo, ou algo para dormir?
Patient: Não, nunca usei nada disso. Não bebo, não fumo, e não tomo qualquer tipo de droga. O médico da escola disse que era ansiedade.
Doctor: Bem, a RM foi limpa, o que já tira alguns pontos. Vamos repassar os exames de sangue que fiz e os resultados já estavam normais. Como o tremor só acontece com esforço e você tem 14 anos, acho que é um tremor cerebelar, uma dessas coisas que vem com o nervosismo, tipo o que a gente chama de tremor essencial ou familial. Mas preciso de certeza, se você tiver mais uma crise forte e o tremor persistir, a gente pode fazer um teste de neurotransmissores para descartar uma causa metabólica ou neurológica mais rara. Por enquanto, o tratamento é fazer fisioterapia e relaxamento, e ver se com o tempo a escola não te dá mais uma chance. Algo mais?
Patient: Não, doutor, obrigado.

Doctor: No, we’ll start with conservative measures. I’m going to prescribe some lubricating drops for the eye, and I’ll show you how to do gentle massage at the corner of her eye. If it doesn’t improve, we have a procedure where we can cauterize the punctum to fix it.

Doctor: Good morning, little man. So, tell me what’s been bothering you since the summer started. Is it your eyes? Patient: Yeah, like... my eyes? They feel heavy? Doctor: Heavy eyes, I see. Do they get red? Watery? Any grittiness? Patient: No, just heavy. Sometimes when I read, they kinda... droop? Like I'm sleepy? Doctor: Droop? As in the lids are hanging down and covering your view? Patient: Yeah, exactly. Not like I can't open them, but they just... hang over my eyes. It's making me trip a bit at school because I can't see my feet. Doctor: I see. And you've had some sun exposure, maybe? And you're growing, right? Any weight changes? Patient: I'm growing taller, that's all. And yeah, been outside a lot. Doctor: Let's take a look. Open wide for me. [examines] Patient: Is he looking at my nose? Doctor: It looks like you've got some extra loose skin over your upper lids. Over time, with sun exposure and growing, the skin just stretches out. It's not your muscles being weak, it's just extra baggy skin. It's called dermatochalasis. Patient: Dermato-what? Doctor: Dermatochalasis. It just means loose skin on the eyelid. It's not your nerve, so you're not really weak, and your eyes aren't rolled in or out. It's just skin. Patient: So it's not like... ptosis? Doctor: No, it's not the muscle that lifts the lid. Your lid margin is right up at the top, it's just got this extra skin that hangs down and partially covers the eye. Very different. Patient: Can I just take a pill? Doctor: No pill for this, I'm afraid. It's just how the skin is. We can try lubricating drops if it's dry, but the main thing is the skin. If it's really bothering your vision and safety, we can talk about a minor procedure to remove that loose skin. For now, keep the sun out with a hat and sunglasses. Patient: Got it. Doctor: Alright, we'll monitor it. Let's check back in six months to see if the skin is getting worse. In the meantime, try not to strain your eyes reading.

S: 55 y/o F presents with acute painless monocular vision loss in the left eye for the past 3 days. She reports a transient episode yesterday of similar left-sided vision loss lasting about 5 minutes that resolved completely. No diplopia, ptosis, or eye pain. No prior ocular or neurologic history. Non-smoker, BMI 33. Family history negative for malignancy or vascular disease. Socially she lives independently.

O: Vitals stable. Pupils: brisk direct and consensual light reflex in the right eye; sluggish direct response in the left with slightly greater anisocoria in dim light than bright. Extraocular movements intact bilaterally. Confrontation visual fields: normal in right eye, dense inferior altitudinal defect in left eye.

Dilated fundoscopy: normal right optic disc with sharp margins and no hemorrhage; left optic disc shows mild pallor of the inferior rim only. Intraocular pressures normal bilaterally. No retinal emboli or hemorrhages.

A: 1) Left optic neuropathy, likely ischemic optic neuropathy (anterior) secondary to transient ischemic attack (TIA) involving the left ophthalmic artery territory.
2) Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
3) Obesity.

P: 1) Admitted to hospital for vascular workup including urgent carotid duplex, echocardiogram with bubble study, and MRI/MRA of head and neck.
2) Initiate low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg nightly.
3) Tight glycemic control; review diabetes medications with endocrinology.
4) Follow-up with neuro-ophthalmology in 1 week for visual field testing and optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the RNFL.

S: ३२ वर्षीय पुरुष रुग्ण डाव्या कर्णापेक्षा उजवा कान जास्त चांगला ऐकू शकतो असे सांगत आला आहे. हा त्रास त्याला जन्मापासूनच (since birth) आहे, पण कानात कधीही इन्फेक्शन झाले नाही किंवा डोक्याला कधी दुखापत झाली नाही. त्याला सध्या कोणताही त्रास, चक्कर (dizziness) किंवा ओटिटिस मीडिया विथ इफ्यूजन (OME) ची लक्षणे नाहीत. तो त्याच्या कार्यालयात (office) काम करतो आणि त्याला या समस्येचा त्याच्या दैनंदिन कामावर कोणताही परिणाम झालेला वाटत नाही. तो खूप मोठ्या आवाजात इअरफोन्स (earphones) वापरल्याचाही इन्कार करतो. प्रसूतीपूर्व (prenatal) संगोपन चाचण्या किंवा जन्माच्या वेळी झालेल्या गुंतागुंतीबद्दल कोणतीही माहिती उपलब्ध नाही.

O: उजव्या कानाचा TM (tympanic membrane) आणि canal स्पष्ट दिसत आहे, कानाच्या मेण (cerumen) ची साधी स्वच्छता केली. ट्यूनिंग फोर्क (512Hz) वापरून वेबर (Weber) आणि रिन्ने (Rinne) चाचण्या केल्या. आवाज उजव्या कानाकडे झुकतो. फिंगर रब (finger rub) चाचणी करताना डाव्या कानी ऐकू येणारा आवाज उजव्या कानापेक्षा खूप कमी होता. दोन्ही कानांची ओटोस्कोपी (otoscopy) सामान्य आहे. ओटोअकौस्टिक एमिशन्स (OAEs) चाचणी केली, ज्यामध्ये दोन्ही कानांचा प्रतिसाद कमी/अनुपस्थित (low/absent) दिसला, तर उजव्या कानाचा रिस्पॉन्स (ABR) थोडा चांगला होता. हे निष्कर्ष (findings) बाल्यावस्थेपासून चालत आलेल्या द्विपक्षीय (bilateral), कोणत्याही ज्ञात संसर्गजन्य किंवा संरचनात्मक (structural) कारण नसलेल्या कानाच्या समस्येशी सुसंगत आहेत.

A: रुग्णामध्ये जन्मापासूनच (congenital) असलेल्या, कारण आणि प्रकार (conductive vs sensorineural) अजून स्पष्ट न झालेल्या श्रवणदोषाचे निदान (diagnosis). रुग्णाचे ऑडिओमेट्री (audiometry) आणि क्लिनिकल कोरिलेशन (clinical correlation) करणे सुरू आहे.

P: १. ENT तज्ज्ञाकडे (ENT specialist) पुढील ऑडिओमेट्री (audiometry) आणि क्लिनिकल मूल्यांकनासाठी (clinical evaluation) संदर्भ.
२. कानाला कोणताही आघात (trauma) किंवा जास्त आवाजापासून संरक्षण (noise protection) करण्यासाठी रुग्णाला सल्ला दिला. आवश्यकतेनुसार हियरिंग एड (hearing aid) किंवा असिस्टिव्ह लिसनिंग डिव्हाइस (ALD) वापरण्याबद्दल तज्ज्ञांच्या मार्गदर्शनाखाली चर्चा केली जाईल.

Patient: ৪০ বছর বয়সী বিবাহিতা মহিলা, গত ৪ মাস ধরে ক্রমাগত মাথা ঘোরার সমস্যা নিয়ে ওপিডি-তে এসেছেন।

S:

O:

নিউরো: ফান্ডি এবং ক্রেনিয়াল নার্ভ স্বাভাবিক। মাথা নাড়াতে কোনো নিস্টাগমাস নেই। ডিসডায়ডকোকাইনেসিয়া এবং রোমবার্গ টেস্ট স্বাভাবিক। চোখে ভেতরের দিকের চোখের পলক ছাড়া অন্য কোনো অস্বাভাবিকতা নেই। কালস টেস্টে পজিটিভ নেই।

A:
ক্রনিক ভেস্টিবুলার সিনড্রোম, আনস্পেসিফাইড (Chronic vestibular syndrome, unspecified)।

P:
১. ভেস্টিবুলার ফিজিওথেরাপি (Vestibular rehabilitation therapy) চালিয়ে যাওয়ার পরামর্শ এবং ঘুমের রুটিন ঠিক রাখা।

S: 14 বছর বয়সী ছেলে, মূল অভিযোগ: দীর্ঘস্থায়ী কান ভরা ভাব, বারবার কানে পপ শব্দ হওয়া (ear popping) এবং ডান কানে ক্র্যাকল (crackling) শব্দ। গত ৩ মাস ধরে লক্ষণগুলো চলছে, মাঝে মাঝে স্বতঃস্ফূর্তভাবে ঠিক হয়ে যায়। কান থেকে কোনো তরল বা রক্ত বের হচ্ছে না। কোনো মাথা ঘোরা (vertigo) নেই। Tmj টিএমজে (TMJ) সমস্যা নিয়েও অভিযোগ আছে, তবে এর সাথে এর কোনো সম্পর্ক নেই।

O: ডান কান পরীক্ষা: Tympanic membrane (TM) একদম স্বাভাবিক, কোনো রিট্রাকশন বা ওটিটিস মিডিয়া নেই, মোবিলিটি স্বাভাবিক। Left TM normal। Inspection of nasopharynx: Pharyngeal mucosa পরিষ্কার, কোনো ফোলা বা পুঁজ নেই। Cleft palate negative।

A: Right-sided eustachian tube diverticulum.

P: 1) Right-sided eustachian tube diverticulum-এর জন্য conservative management: saline nasal spray, TMJ exercises, steam inhalation।
2) ENT specialist-এর সাথে follow-up 4-6 সপ্তাহ পর।
3) Patulous eustachian tube-এর জন্য কোনো intervention-এর প্রয়োজন নেই কারণ রোগীর কানে কোনো একটানা echoing বা autophony নেই। Eustachian salpingitis বা purulent discharge-এর কোনো প্রমাণ নেই।

Pt 58m. hx 1yr L-sided tinnitus, progressive aural fullness. Exam: L-sided tuning fork (Rinne pos, Weber L), normal VOR gains in yaw (head impulse neg), no nystagmus nav. MRI IAC: 2.1 cm L-sided vestibular schwannoma. Tx: ENT referral for neurotology, neurosurgery consult. Dx: LSS schwannoma.

Doctor: So, Sarah, you mentioned on the scheduler that your daughter is having a lot of trouble with writing. Let's talk about that today. Patient: Yes, she's 8 years old and in third grade. She just gets so frustrated every night with homework. Doctor: Can you tell me what the homework looks like for her? Patient: They have these paragraphs where she has to write a personal narrative about her weekend. She takes two hours, her handwriting is a mess, and she cries when I ask her to do it. Doctor: I see. And what happens at school? Do the teachers say anything? Patient: Her teacher called me last week. She's doing okay in math and reading, but she refuses to do any writing assignments. The teacher said she spells things correctly when she's talking, but on paper she just writes a few words and then stops. She says her thoughts move faster than her hand can keep up. Doctor: Have you noticed if she avoids writing in other areas, like copying notes from the board? Patient: Oh, totally. Even when she's copying a sentence from the book, she just draws little squiggles at the back of the page so she doesn't have to write. Doctor: I appreciate you giving me these details. It sounds a lot like a developmental learning disorder, specifically she's struggling significantly with written expression. Her reading and math seem to be on track, and her oral language is fine, so it's not a general language issue or a math disability. We're going to do some formal testing on her writing fluency, spelling, and handwriting motor skills to get a clear picture, and we can look into accommodations like a keyboarding program or a scribe. In the meantime, give her a little grace, but try to keep her writing practice to just ten to fifteen minutes a night so she doesn't get overwhelmed. We'll follow up once we have the results from the educational psychologist. Patient: Okay, thank you, that helps.

Doctor: So tell me again about the hearing problem. Patient: It's right ear, been bothering me for a couple of months. Sound like there's a radio on in my head all the time. Can't hear my wife when there's background noise like the TV or the dishwasher. My GP mentioned maybe it was wax or something growing in the ear canal. But it's not like that, he's checked it twice. It's high pitched, almost like a squeal, and it's definitely not coming from outside. Doctor: Okay. Since it started, have you been working at the plant or doing anything with loud machinery? Patient: Yeah, I'm on the floor, lots of metal grinding, saws, compressors. Earplugs but sometimes I forget them. Doctor: Any pain, dizziness, ear fullness, or drainage? Patient: No pain, no dizziness. Ear doesn't feel full. No fluid. Just this constant Phantom ringing after shifts. Doctor: Alright. I'm looking at your ears now and the drum looks fine, no redness, no wax, no fluid. The ringing seems to be originating from inside. Based on your history and the fact that the exam is otherwise normal, this is consistent with noise exposure causing inner ear damage. We aren't seeing an infection, a tumor, or anything structural on the scan I ordered. I want you to wear those custom earplugs I gave you, and we can refer you to hearing specialists for hearing aids if the noise is still bad after your break next month. Any questions? Patient: No, thanks doc.

Exam: negative Dix-Hallpike, no nystagmus, gait stable. ENT/Audiogram: WNL, MRI brain/internal auditory canals: negative. Dx: BPPV, posterior canal. Plan: Epley maneuver today. Stop antihistamines. Return if persisting >2w.

M. Dupont, 68 ans : Tinnitus gauche, surdité progressive unilatérale gauche. En ERG, absence de VBL et onde III sur BOA gauche. AOM gauche +. Diagn. Névrite auditive gauche. Traité par prednisone 1 mg/kg. Suivi en ORL.

S: রোগী একজন প্রাপ্তবয়স্ক মহিলা (৪৫ বছর), গত ৬ মাস ধরে ডান কানে হালকা শ্রবণশক্তি হ্রাস এবং কানে ভারী অনুভূতির কথা জানায়। কান থেকে কোনো স্রাব বা রক্তপাত নেই। কোনো ব্যথা বা মাথা ঘোরার কথা অস্বীকার করেছে। আগে কখনো কান পুরাপুরি বন্ধ হয়ে যাওয়ার সমস্যা হয়নি।
O: ডান কানের পিনি (Pinna) নরমাল। ডান কানের নালি (External Auditory Canal) পরিষ্কার, কোনো ইনডেক্স বা ইমপ্যাকশন নেই। টিম্প্যানিক মেমব্রেন (Tympanic membrane) গ্রেড ২ রিট্রাকশন দেখায়, হালকা সেরাস ফ্লুইড লেভেল দেখা যাচ্ছে। ম্যালিয়াস (Malleus) দৃশ্যমান এবং নরমাল। বাম কানের পরীক্ষা নরমাল। পুওর ভিলিয়ামস (Whisper test) ডান কানে +২।

A: ১. ক্রনিক সেরাস বা মিউকয়েড ওটিটিস মিডিয়া (Chronic serous/mucoid otitis media) - ডান কান।
২. সেন্সরিনিউরাল হিয়ারিং লস (Sensorineural hearing loss) - ডান কান (সম্ভবত নন-স্পেসিফিক সেন্সরিনিউরাল হিয়ারিং লস)।

P: ১. ডান কানের জন্য অলিভ অয়েল (Olive oil) বা অরাল কেয়ার ড্রপস (ural care eardrops) দিনে ২ বার করে ২ সপ্তাহের জন্য দেওয়া হলো, যা কানের ময়লা নরম করতে সাহায্য করবে।
২. কানের প্রেসার স্বাভাবিক করতে এবং ফ্লুইড সাবলিঙ্গুয়ালি (sublingually) শুষে নিতে রাইন্যাল টিউব (Eustachian tube) প্যাটেন্সি বজায় রাখার জন্য নাসাল স্যালাইন স্প্রে (Nasal saline spray) দিনে ২ বার।
৩. ১ মাস পর অডিওলজি (Audiology) এবং ইএনটি (ENT) ক্লিনিকে রিভিউ। যদি তাতেও উন্নতি না হয়, তবে টিম্পানোস্টমি টিউব (Tympanostomy tube) বা মাইক্রো-ইনসিশন / গ্রোমেট (Grommet) সন্নিবেশনের কথা বিবেচনা করা হবে।
৪. বর্তমান সমস্যা ছাড়া অন্য কোনো উল্লেখযোগ্য মেডিকেল হিস্ট্রি নেই। রোগীর জন্য কোনো অ্যান্টিবায়োটিকের প্রয়োজন নেই (ABx not indicated)।

S: 17 y/o F presents with 3-day hx of sharp, pleuritic chest pain that worsens lying supine and on inspiration, with relief when leaning forward. Denies fever, cough, or URI sx. Reports recent participation in competitive volleyball with 2-3 recent head-to-head contact episodes 1 mo ago. Denies recent travel, sick contacts, or sick pets. No prior hx of chest pain, syncope, or hx of rheumatic fever. No PMH of cardiac Tx or immunosuppression. Denies palpitations, orthopnea, or DOE.

O: Vitals: afebrile, HR 98, RR 14, BP 100/65, SpO2 98% RA. Exam: Pericardial friction rub heard at left lower sternal border, early diastolic. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Lungs clear. Extremities warm, no edema. Neuro exam non-focal. EKG: Diffuse concave ST elevation in all limb leads with PR segment depression in II, III, aVF, V4-V6. Echo: Small pericardial effusion, LVEF 60%, no wall motion abnormalities.

A: 1. Acute pericarditis, unspecified - meets classic criteria: pleuritic chest pain, CT elevation, pericardial rub, and no evidence of infection, malignancy, or myocardial injury on echo.

2. Exertional somatic chest wall pain, secondary - pain likely exacerbated by recent contact sport; considered costochondritis.

P: 1. NSAIDs: Ibuprofen 600 mg PO q6h PRN pain/fever. Taper over 2-3 weeks.
2. Colchicine 0.5 mg PO BID x 3 months.
3. Strict rest from competitive volleyball for 4-6 weeks; avoid heavy contact.
4. Follow-up with Cardiology in 1 week for repeat EKG.
5. Consider Work-up for TB, Coxsackie, Coxsackie, HIV if persistent or recurrent.

S: 5 साल की FEMALE बालिका को 2 दिन से बार-बार palpitations और धड़कन तेज होने की शिकायत के साथ लाया गया है। माता-पिता ने बताया कि पिछले 3-4 एपिसोड में बच्चा अचानक रोने लगता है, उसकी त्वचा पीली पड़ जाती है और वह बहुत सुस्त हो जाता है। एपिसोड अचानक शुरू होते हैं और 5-10 मिनट बाद अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं। कोई syncope या सांस फूलने का इतिहास नहीं है। जन्म के समय फिक्स हार्ट मर्मर के लिए CABG (congenital anomaly) का इतिहास है, अन्यथा बच्चा स्वस्थ है। कोई बुखार या URTI के लक्षण नहीं हैं। AEDs का कोई घरेलू उपयोग नहीं है।

O: Vitals: Temp 36.8°C, HR 85 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 100%.
Exam: Alert, oriented, hemodynamically stable. Heart: S1 और S2 नॉर्मल हैं, कोई मर्मर या गैलॉप नहीं। Lung fields क्लियर हैं। Abdomen नर्म है। Neuro: नॉर्मल।

ECG ( ambulatory monitoring / Holter के आधार पर): एपिसोड के दौरान 240 bpm की नियमित narrow complex tachycardia, P waves का न होना, ST-T में थोड़ा बदलाव। कोई delta waves (WPW) या pre-excitation स्पष्ट नहीं है।

EKG (sinus rhythm के दौरान): छोटा PR interval, कोई स्पष्ट delta waves नहीं।

Echo: 2D echo नॉर्मल है, LV और RV नॉर्मल साइज में हैं। कोई structural CHD नहीं।

A: 1. Atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia (AVRT), unspecified (WPW नहीं)।
Diastolic murmur / fixed split S2 का इतिहास मौजूद है, जो repaired CABG/CHD के कारण हो सकता है।

P: 1. Cardiology referral और Electrophysiology (EP) study के लिए OT बुक करें।
2. 24-hour ambulatory ECG monitoring (Holter) शुरू करें।
3. माता-पिता को SVT episode के दौरान vagal maneuvers (जैसे Valsalva maneuver) करने के लिए शिक्षित करें।
4. Electrolytes और CBC नॉर्मल हैं, कोई दवा नहीं दी गई है।

S: 8-year-old F presents with 12h history of sudden onset right arm pain, pallor, and pulselessness of the right hand. Symptoms began acutely at school. No prior history of vascular disease or clotting disorder. No recent trauma, surgery, or central lines. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath. No significant past problems. No recent travel. No family history of thrombosis.

O: Vitals stable. On exam, the right upper extremity is visibly pale and cool compared to the left. No palpable radial or brachial pulses on the right. Capillary refill >4 sec on the right fingers. Allen's test demonstrates absent ulnar flow on the right. Sensation intact, but right hand is painful to passive stretch. No cyanosis or mottling. Left extremity normal. CXR clear. ECG normal sinus rhythm.

A: Acute upper limb arterial occlusion, unspecified.

P: 1. Immediate vascular surgery and cardiology consults for surgical exploration and possible embolectomy or thrombectomy. 2. Monitor neurovascular status of the right hand closely with serial exams and Doppler studies.
3. Pain control and limb elevation. 4. Admit to floor for observation and workup. 5. DVT prophylaxis with enoxaparin pending surgical evaluation. 6. Rule out underlying hypercoagulable state and underlying cardiac source.

S: Patient de 68 ans, homme, consulte pour fatigue et sensation de battement du cœur rapide ces 2 semaines. Antécédents: HTA diagnostiquée il y a 3 ans, suivi par cardiologue. Pas de dyslipidémie. Tabagisme: ancien (30 paquets/an, arrêté il y a 5 ans). Pas de consommation d'alcool. Pas d'antécédent de ictus ni d'infarctus. Pas de diabète. Pas d'antécédents familiaux de cardiopathie. Pas de médicaments actuels.
O: HR 88/min, FR 16/min, PA 168/98 mmHg (doigt, gauche, assis). Poids 92 kg, IMC 30,1. Pas d'œdème des membres inférieurs. Auscultation: ondes T inversées en V3-V4, bruit S4 discret. Échocardiogramme: LVH avec EF 55%. Pas d'éjection de masse. Pas de rétrécissement mitral ni d'insuffisance. Pas d'arythmie au monitorage de 24h.
A: Hypertension artérielle artérielle combinée (systolique et diastolique). Modification de l'antihypertenseur actuel (perindopril 4 mg). Commencer candésartan 16 mg/hctz 12,5 mg. Échocardiogramme de surveillance dans 6 mois. Pas de preuve d'hypertension isolée (systolique ou diastolique), ni d'HTA essentielle non spécifiée.
P: Continuez l'amoxicilline-acidulée pour bronchite aiguë (traitement en cours depuis 5 jours). Éviter le sel. Pratiquer une activité physique modérée. Contrôle PA dans 1 mois. Pas de SARM n'est indiquée.
Date: 15/10/2024

S: ६८ वर्षीय पुरुष, ४ दिवसांपासून प्रगतीशील डिस्पनिया, ऑर्थोपनिया आणि थकवा. सुरुवातीला अँटीबायोटिक्सने उपचार केलेल्या अप्पर रेस्पिरेटरी ट्रॅक्ट इन्फेक्शनची हिस्ट्री. अलीकडे एक नवीन अँटीहिस्टामाइन सुरू केले होते. ॲलर्जीची कोणतीही ज्ञात हिस्ट्री नाही. मस्कुलोस्केलेटल छातीत दुखणे.
O: व्हिटॅल्स: BP १२५/८० mmHg, HR ९२ bpm, RR २२ /min, SpO2 ९४% on RA. JVP उंचावले, S3 गॅलॉप. २+ परिफेरल पिटिंग एडिमा. लंग्ज: क्रॅकल्स खालील लोब्समध्ये. EKG: डिफ्यूज ST डिप्रेशन आणि लो व्होल्टेज QRS. इको: EF ४५%, ग्लोबल हायपोकायनेसिस, कोणतेही विशिष्ट वॉल मोशन ॲबनॉर्मॅलिटी नाही. लॅब: Troponin I ०.१२ ng/mL mildly elevated. CBC: WCC १४.५, Eosinophils १२% (absolute २.२ x १०^९/L). CRP १२० mg/L. इन्फेक्शियस वर्कअप: निगेटिव्ह रक्त संस्कृती, EBV/CMV IgM/IgG निगेटिव्ह, COVID-19 PCR निगेटिव्ह.
A: हायपरसेन्सिटिव्हिटी मायोकार्डायटिस.
P: १. नवीन अँटीहिस्टामाइन औषध तात्काळ थांबवले. २. हाय-डोस IV मिथाइलप्रेडनिसोलोन (१ mg/kg/day) सुरू केले. ३. डायुरेटिक थेरपी (furosemide ४० mg/day) सुरू केली. ४. हायपरसेन्सिटिव्हिटीच्या पुष्टीसाठी कार्डियाक MRI नियोजित. ५. कार्डिओलॉजी फॉलो-अप आणि सीरम इओसिनोफिल मॉनिटरिंग.

नोंद: हा क्लिनिकल चित्र मोठ्या सेल मायोकार्डायटिस (Giant cell myocarditis) किंवा तीव्र संसर्गजन्य मायोकार्डायटिस (Infectious myocarditis) च्या लक्षणांशी जुळत नाही, कारण सिस्टिमिक इन्फेक्शनचा अभाव आणि इओसिनोफिलिया स्पष्ट आहे. रिउमॅटिक मायोकार्डायटिसची (Rheumatic myocarditis) कोणतीही हिस्ट्री, जॉइंट पेन किंवा RF/ASO टायटर्स नाहीत. त्यामुळे हायपरसेन्सिटिव्हिटी/ड्रग-इंड्युस्ड मायोकार्डायटिस हे मुख्य निदान (Target) आहे.

S: Paciente feminina, 45 anos, refere gestação normal, gravida 2, parous 2 (GP 2), sem maus hábitos. Apresentou queixa de palpitações há 3 meses, episódicos, início súbito, paroxismo de taquicardia que se autolimita após 30-60 min, associadas a taquipneia leve e disfunção do dia. Nenhuma sintomatologia de desmaio ou dor torácica. MEDICAÇÃO: metoprolol 25 mg 2x/dia, com alívio parcial. NINGUÉM: tabagismo, hipertensão arterial, DM, AVC. ABNORMALIDADE CARDÍACA: sem cirurgia cardíaca prévia. SINOUS RHYTHM na EKG durante o monitoramento ambulatorial.

O: Eletrocardiograma de 12 derivações: FA normal, QRS estreito (80 ms), AXIS normal, QTc de 420 ms, QRS sem blocos ou WOLFF-PARKINSON-WHITE. Microonda na FA e FV. Eletrocardiograma de 12 derivações após 24h do monitoramento ambulatorial: FA em ritmo sinus, QRS estreito. A: Diagnóstico de Taquicardia Arritmóica Atrial dependente do Istmo Cavotricuspid (CTI-Tachycardia). Ataques são paroxísticos, com início abrupto e término espontâneo, e manobras vagais (masagem do pescoço, Valsalva) conseguem interrupção ou retardamento da frequência. O padrão de ECG durante o evento mostra eje frontal -40, QRS estreito, sem WBW, e ausência de blocos intraventriculares. Com base na topografia do ECG e na epidemiologia (mulher jovem, sem cirurgia cardíaca prévia nem DAH), hypothesis principal é reentrada macrocircuito dependente do istmo cavotricuspid (CTI-dependent macroreentry). Differential: Taquicardia Atrial Macroreentrante (macro reentrant AT), não-isthmus-dependente (ex: macro reentrant AT oclusa ao GA com flutter atrial com flutter atrial ou ao septo interatrial com flutter intra-atrial) - menos provável por causa do eje frontal e ausência de DAH/cirurgia.
