Doctor: Quand vous vous levez, vous tombez vraiment ou vous vous apprêtez à tomber ?
Patient: Non, non, je parviens à me rattraper à la table ou à une chaise. Mais c'est vertigineux, c'est très désagréable.
Doctor: Et y a-t-il un soulagement en vous rasseoir, en continuant de marcher un peu ?
Patient: Oui, tout s'arrête. La sensation de vide disparaît dès que je suis assise à nouveau.
Doctor: Et comment ça se passe la nuit, avec des réveils pour uriner ?
Patient: C'est la même chose, Docteur. Au milieu de la nuit, je me lève pour le petit-déjeuner, et puis là aussi, je ne vois plus rien, j'ai mal au cœur.
Doctor: Avez-vous été diagnostiquée pour une tension artérielle basse en position assise ?
Patient: Non, je n'ai jamais fait de bilan complet sur la tension.
Doctor: D'accord Madame. Je vais faire une prise de tension à jeun, d'abord bien assise bien calme. Puis je vais la refaire en position couchée. Ensuite, nous allons faire un bilan orthostatique. C'est-à-dire que je vais mesurer votre tension chaque minute pendant que vous resterez debout. Je veux vérifier une chute de tension et une accélération du cœur quand vous vous levez.
Patient: D'accord Docteur.
Doctor: Je vais également vous demander de réaliser un ECG, il faut faire une recherche d'arythmie. Enfin, il faut aussi faire un bilan sanguin pour exclure une anémie ou un problème de glycémie.
Patient: Parlez-moi de l'hypotension orthostatique, Docteur ?
Doctor: C'est simple Madame. Quand vous vous levez, le sang n'arrive pas assez vite aux vaisseaux du cerveau. À cause de cela, la pression baisse et votre organisme réagit en accélérant la fréquence cardiaque. C'est ce qu'on appelle l'hypotension orthostatique. C'est la raison pour laquelle vos yeux deviennent noir, vous avez la sensation de faiblir et de tête vide.
Doctor: Pour le traitement, je vais vous prescrire un peu plus de liquide. Il faut boire environ deux litres et demi par jour. Je vais aussi prescrire une augmentation de votre prise de sel, vous pourrez manger des olives, du jambon, du bouillon de volaille, et surtout, vous ne devez plus lever la tête trop vite. Il faut lever les pieds d'abord, puis le thorax, puis la tête. Cela permet de laisser au sang le temps de circuler. Je vous prescris une surveillance de votre tension si possible à domicile.
Patient: Quand est-ce que je pourrai avoir le résultat de votre bilan ?
Doctor: Je vous appelle dès que j'ai les résultats du bilan orthostatique.
Doctor: Prenez soin de vous Madame.

Doctor: Welcome, I'm Dr. Evans. I know it's been a long week of tests and questions for you and your wife, so I want to make sure we talk through today's results clearly. I know you asked about the lung biopsy you had last month. The pathologist looked at the tissue carefully, and the main finding points to an issue with how the tiny air sacs in the lungs make their natural surface fluid, the stuff that keeps the lungs from collapsing. So really, the main concern right now is a disorder of surfactant metabolism. We can talk about how that happens and what it means for your breathing going forward. Patient: So, what exactly is surfactant? I mean, is this something I was born with, or did this happen later? Doctor: That's a great question. For most people, this is a genetic condition you're born with; your body makes an abnormal form of the surfactant protein. It's not something you did or caught later in life. It's not related to infection or fluid buildup in the lymphatic channels, and it's not a pattern of lung disease that looks like the other specific interstitial conditions we see in kids. It's specifically about the structure of the surfactant itself. Patient: Are there other conditions that look like this? Could it be confused with the other lung problems we read about online? Doctor: I understand the concern. We actually ruled out a few things on our differential. It's not chronic pneumonitis of infancy, because you're an adult, and the biopsy doesn't show that particular inflammation. It's also not neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia, alveolar proteinosis, or any of the developmental disorders or lymphatic dysplasia syndromes. The biopsy shows abnormal lamellar bodies consistent with a metabolic error in surfactant turnover. Patient: So what's the plan? Doctor: We're going to get genetic testing to confirm which gene is involved, and then we'll start you on a trial of aerosolized surfactant replacement therapy. We'll monitor your oxygen levels and do another high-resolution CT in three months to see how the lungs respond.

Doctor: Hi, come on in. I'm reading through the intake forms. I see your main issue is hives. What brings you in today?
Patient: It's been this for about six months now. If someone scratches my arm or even just presses a pen against my skin, these lines pop up exactly where they touched. It's not a bug bite or anything like that.
Doctor: And how long does it last?
Patient: Usually it fades within ten to fifteen minutes. It itches like crazy while it's there, but no swelling of my lips or tongue.
Doctor: Are there any other triggers you've noticed, like cold air or tight clothing?
Patient: No, nothing like that. It's purely mechanical. It's really embarrassing at school when I'm sitting at my desk and the side of the chair leaves a mark and then I get these weals.
Doctor: Let me take a look at one of your arms.
Patient: Here, try it. Just press your thumb right there.
Doctor: [Presses thumb on forearm] Okay, I can see you're developing the classic lines now.
Patient: See? It's not even been two minutes.
Doctor: Alright, so this is what we call dermographism. It's basically a physical urticaria where your skin literally writes messages on itself in response to pressure or scratching. We can rule out the other triggers like cold or delayed pressure reactions because this is immediate and mechanical. Have you ever had a bad reaction to a specific cream or lotion touching your skin?
Patient: No, just this pressure thing.
Doctor: Okay, great. So I'm going to diagnose this as dermographism, a type of inducible urticaria. It's generally benign, though annoying. I'll prescribe a daily non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine to take as needed and for prevention. Also, loose cotton clothing and avoiding tight belts might help. Does that sound okay?

S: 15-year-old male presents with progressive ulnar drift of the ring and little fingers, associated with clawing of the 4th and 5th digits. Denies acute trauma; reports gradual onset over ~3 months, initially noted as difficulty with zipping backpack. No nocturnal pain. Denies any recent injections, infections, or systemic autoimmune symptoms. PMH: Lacks 4th and 5th fingers on right hand since birth, otherwise healthy.

O: Examination reveals a 4th and 5th digit claw deformity bilaterally. The 4th digit shows metacarpophalangeal hyperextension with interphalangeal flexion; the 5th digit is similarly affected. Ulnar drift noted at the metacarpophalangeal joints with 15-degree deviation. Grip strength decreased by ~40% compared to baseline. No swelling or erythema over joints. No sensory deficits in the distribution of the ulnar or median nerves. Normal tendon reflexes. No evidence of wrist drop, radial deviation, or equinovalgus deformity.

A: 1. Acquired clawhand, bilateral (4th and 5th digits). Differential includes ulnar nerve palsy; however, this presentation is more consistent with an intrinsic muscle imbalance (interossei/lumbrical weakness) rather than a peripheral nerve lesion. Recommending EMG/NCS in 6 weeks if no improvement with protective splinting.

P: 1. Initiate night splints for MCP joint positioning to prevent progressive flexion contractures. 2. Occupational therapy for fine motor exercises and grip strengthening. 3. Follow-up in 4 weeks to assess fit and function of splints. 4. If no structural improvement, refer to orthopedics for surgical options (e.g., intrinsic muscle transfer). 5. Patient counseled on safe activities of daily living to avoid further strain.

68M: 3d FU knee pain, fever. 48h x-ray normal. MRI: T7/T8 paravertebral/epidural enhancement. Labs: Hb 11.2, neutrophilic leukocytosis 14.5. Blood cultures pending. Dx: acute haematogenous osteomyelitis. Admit, IV vanco. Exclude spinal epidural abscess.

Doctor: Good morning. I have your labs from yesterday. The uric acid is very high at 12.5. I also see you’ve been having occasional tophi on the fingers and elbow. Have you noticed any attacks of intense swelling, redness, and excruciating pain, particularly in a big toe or knee?

Patient: Oh yes, they come on suddenly. The last one two weeks ago woke me up at 3 a.m. My right knee was swollen, shiny, and I couldn’t bend it. I had to walk with a cane for a week. The blood work also showed low uric acid in the urine, and sometimes the urine is foamy? I think my father had similar issues with tophi, and his was linked to a genetic kidney issue?

Doctor: That lines up with a hereditary metabolic problem. I don’t want to rule out an acquired cause like heavy metal exposure or a diuretic, but your history and the family pattern points to a primary enzyme defect rather than a secondary trigger. So, your gouty arthropathy is due to enzyme defects or other inherited disorders. We don’t need to look for lead exposure or medication causes right now.

Patient: Okay, so this isn’t from a medication or lead?

Doctor: Correct, it is from a genetic enzyme issue causing the genetic form of hyperuricemia.

Patient: Got it, thanks.

Doctor: We’ll start colchicine for the flares and begin allopurinol for long-term management. Also, check your blood pressure and cholesterol since this tends to cluster with metabolic syndrome.

Patient: Sounds good, I’ll check next week.

Doctor: Perfect. See you then.

S:
10-year-old male presents with chronic, progressive stiffness and swelling of the right knee. He is a known diabetic, HbA1c 9.8% on metformin. History of peripheral neuropathy. Denies acute trauma or hemarthrosis. Denies recent rashes or allergic reactions to antibiotics/NSAIDs.

O:
Exam: Right knee with non-tender, boggy effusion, limited passive ROM to 0-110 degrees. No erythema or warmth. Left knee normal. Sensation intact to light touch; pain-free proprioception. X-ray right knee: moderate joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, marginal osteophytes. Labs: HgbA1c 9.8%, CRP 0.4. RF negative, ANA negative, CBC normal, no evidence of bleeding diathesis.

A:
1. Diabetic arthropathy.
2. Uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus.

P:
- Continue metformin; start basal insulin nightly and optimize glucose control (target 80-130 fasting).
- PT referral for knee strengthening and ROM exercises.
- NSAIDs PRN for pain/swelling; avoid intra-articular steroids if possible due to infection risk.
- Re-image in 12 months to monitor progression.
- Consider orthopedic surgery review if mechanical symptoms (catching/locking) develop.

65yo F presents with worsening dyspareunia and sensation of obstruction during intercourse, more pronounced in dorsal recumbent. No vaginal or introital laxity/numbness. Exam: Grade II cystocele. Dx: Obstructed intercourse. Pessary fitting, pelvic floor physio, lubricants.

Doctor: नमस्कार, आज काय त्रास आहे? Patient: मला सतत खूप गरम होतंय. Doctor: किती दिवसांपासून आहे हे? Patient: गेल्या काही महिन्यांपासून. Doctor: काही रात्री झोप लागण्यात अडचण येतेय का? Doctor: आपण काही बेसिक टेस्ट करून घेऊ. Patient: चालेल डॉक्टर. Doctor: इस्ट्रोजेनची पातळी तपासण्यासाठी रक्त तपासणी करू, जेणेकरून आपण पुढचा उपचार ठरवू शकू. Patient: नक्कीच.

S: 56 y/o male presents for routine nephrology follow-up. He has a long-standing history of well-controlled hypertension. He denies any symptoms of fluid overload, dysuria, or gross hematuria. He reports good adherence to lisinopril 10 mg daily and amlodipine 5 mg daily. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or IV drug use. No family history of renal failure or polycystic kidney disease.
P: BP: 128/78. HR: 68. No edema. No costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis: 1+ protein, no blood, no casts. CBC and BMP are within normal limits.
O: Laboratory data from 6 months ago demonstrates an eGFR of 65 mL/min/1.73m^2. Current labs today confirm stable eGFR of 64 mL/min/1.73m^2. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio is 280 mg/g, indicating stage A2 albuminuria. BP has been consistently controlled on current regimen.
A: 1. Chronic kidney disease (CKD), stage 2 (eGFR 60-89 with albuminuria). Stable. Continue ACE-I and maintain BP <130/80. Monitor eGFR and UACR q6 months.
2. Hypertension - controlled on ACE-I.
P: Continue current antihypertensive regimen. Encourage low-sodium diet. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if symptoms develop.

8 yo F presents with 3 mo hx of continuous urinary leakage per vagina. Exam with good lighting shows a combined leak involving bladder, urethra and vagina; catheterization confirms urine tracking from all three sources. U/S to rule out abscess negative. Scheduled for transvaginal repair with urology.

S:
58 y/o male presents with complaint of increased bleeding frequency from the genital region. Patient reports 6 episodes in the past 7 days, with soaking through 3 pads/hour at peak. Associated with mild abdominal cramping but no pelvic pain. No history of recent trauma, surgery, or medication changes. No history of hematuria, melena, or hematemesis. Denies weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Prior stable history includes essential hypertension.

O:
Vitals: BP 138/82, HR 82, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA
Genitourinary: A&D (androgen/dysovulatory) female phenotype confirmed by exam; external genitalia shows active oozing blood from a proliferative-phase-like endometrium; no masses, no lesions, no cervical friability. No organ involvement elsewhere. Skin: clear.
Labs: Hgb 10.2 g/dL (down from 11.8 on prior visit 4 months ago), Hct 30.4%, MCV 84 fL, TSH 1.9 uIU/mL, PT/INR 1.0.

A:
Abnormal frequency of uterine bleeding, unspecified.

P:
1. Iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID) to correct borderline anemia.
2. Pelvic US scheduled in 2 weeks to rule out structural etiology (polyps, adenomyosis) and to stage the endometrium; no active mass seen on exam today to explain the excessive volume.
3. Continue current antihypertensive regimen.
4. Return to ED for any syncope, hemodynamic instability, or passage of large clots.

S:
Paciente feminina, 62 anos, busca por dificuldade para manter a lubrificação vaginal durante a atividade sexual. Relata que na maioria das vezes não consegue manter a lubrificação e precisa de auxílio lubrificante, o que causa desconforto e evitação da atividade sexual. Não apresenta histórico de trauma sexual ou ginecológico significativo. Última menarca aos 55 anos. Acompanhada do conviva, que rapporte que a paciente evita a relação íntima. 1 semana de dificuldade. Não toma medicação que possa estar associada.

O:
Exame pélvico: epitélio vaginal maduro, pH 4.5, ausência de secreções patológicas. Padronização de padroeira GOLDSTEIN negativa. Ausência de estrias ou atrofia. Banda de pH normal. Exame neurológico, cardiovascular e metabólico normais.


A:
Disfunção da excitação sexual feminina, não especificada.


P:
Iniciada terapia comportamental sexual: orientação à estimulação clitoral e vulvar e uso de lubrificantes à base de água. Prescrita estradiol transdérmico 50 mcg/dia (se एप्लीcado, com avaliação de risco). Agendado retorno em 8 semanas.


Histórico relevante: Hipertensão arterial essencial. (Não relacionada àcurrentCharacter atual do atendimento).

S: 14 वर्षीय पुरुष, पिछले 6 महीनों से कमर के निचले हिस्से (low back) में तेज दर्द की शिकायत। दर्द ज्यादातर मासिक धर्म (menstrual) के दौरान और उसके आसपास बढ़ जाता है। कोई मतली (nausea), उल्टी (vomiting) या आंतों की आदतों में कोई बदलाव नहीं। पेशाब ठीक से हो रहा है। कोई बुखार या वज़न घटना नहीं। कोई ज्ञात जन्मजात बीमारी नहीं।

O: शारीरिक जाँच (Physical exam) में, रीढ़ और रीढ़ की हड्डियों (spine) की जाँच सामान्य है। पेल्विक (pelvic) जाँच के दौरान आगे (anterior) से कोई दर्द नहीं है। पेल्विस के अंदरूनी हिस्से (pelvic exam) में गर्भाशय (uterus) सामान्य आकार और दिशा में है। टिप (tip) तक कोई कोमलता (tenderness) नहीं। कोई द्रव्यमान (mass) महसूस नहीं हुआ। पेल्विक अल्ट्रासाउंड रिपोर्ट सामान्य है, कोई सिस्ट (cyst) या अन्य असामान्यता नहीं है।

A: पेल्विक साइड वॉल (pelvic side wall) और रेक्टोवेजाइनल सेप्टम (rectovaginal septum) को छोड़कर, सर्जरी के दौरान यूटेरोसेक्रल लिगामेंट्स (uterosacral ligaments) पर एंडोमेट्रियोसिस (endometriosis) की पुष्टि। यह एक विशिष्ट स्थान (specific site) पर स्थानीयकृत (localized) है।

P: 1. रेटिनोइड (retinoid) थेरेपी (जैसे Isotretinoin 0.5 mg/kg) शुरू करें, जो एंडोमेट्रियोटिक घावों (endometriotic lesions) को सिकोड़ने में सहायक है।
2. दर्द प्रबंधन (Pain management) के लिए हर 8 घंटे में इबुप्रोफेन 400 mg PRN दें।
3. 8 सप्ताह में फॉलो-अप (follow-up) के लिए बुलाएं। यदि 3 महीने में दर्द (pain) में कोई सुधार नहीं होता है, तो GnRH एनालॉग (GnRH analog) पर विचार करें।

Doctor: নমস্কার, ভেতরে আসুন। কী সমস্যা নিয়ে এসেছেন আজকে? Patient: ডাক্তারবাবু, গত তিন মাস ধরে আমার ভারী রক্তপাত হচ্ছে। সাথে পেলভিকের বাম দিকে বেশ ব্যথা, বিশেষ করে প্রস্রাব করার সময়। মাঝে মাঝে যৌন মিলনের সময়ও খুব ব্যথা লাগে। Doctor: আচ্ছা। এই ব্যথাটা ঠিক কোথায় বেশি হয়? Patient: বেশিরভাগ সময় পেটের নিচের বাঁ দিকের দিকে থাকে। ভারী রক্তপাতের কারণে আমাকে মাঝে মাঝেই প্যাড বদলাতে হয়। ডাক্তারবাবু, আমি কি কোনো ক্যানসার বা বড় কোনো অসুখে ভুগছি? Doctor: আমরা কিছু টেস্ট করে দেখব। আল্ট্রাসাউন্ডে আপনার জরায়ুর পেশির ভেতরে endometrial টিস্যুর মতো কিছু ছড়িয়ে পড়তে দেখা যাচ্ছে। এটাকেই আমরা adenomyosis বলি। Patient: এই adenomyosis কী? এতে কি আমার সন্তান ধারণের ক্ষমতা নষ্ট হয়ে যাবে? Doctor: এটা জরায়ুর পেশির ভেতরে টিস্যু বেড়ে যাওয়ার একটা সমস্যা। এতে ভারী রক্তপাত আর পেলভিকের ব্যথা হয়, কিন্তু এটা ক্যানসার নয়। এর ফলে আপনার সন্তানের ক্ষতি হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা নেই। আমরা আপনাকে কিছু ওষুধ দেব যাতে ব্যথা কমে, আর একটা MRI করে দেখতে পারি যে এটা কতটা ছড়িয়েছে।

Doctor: Bom dia. Pode me dizer o que o traz hoje? Patient: Bom dia, doutor. Tenho uma dúvida. Nos últimos dois meses, quando estou com a minha esposa, não consigo conseguir uma ereção firme. A questão é que… acho que é por causa de um conflito que tivemos na família do meu sogro. Patient: Houve uma briga séria. A minha esposa e eu não falávamos a semana inteira. Patient: Ela disse que se eu pudesse mostrar que a valorizo e que não a ignoro, ela ia querer passar mais tempo comigo, e eu acho que essa pressão foi demais. Patient: Devo confessar que, para evitar essa tensão, eu simplesmente… não dava certo. Patient: Mas na verdade eu sei que o problema não é do meu corpo, nem do meu cérebro. Patient: É o que está acontecendo entre nós dois. Patient: O médico da família me disse que devia vir aqui, e eu concordei. Patient: Acho que a proximidade entre nós está afetada, e não consigo me sentir bem quando a gente está juntos. Doctor: Acho que você tem razão. Parece que todo esse stress familiar e essa falta de comunicação conjugal está criando um distanciamento entre vocês dois. Patient: Exatamente, doutor. Doctor: Vamos registrar isso como uma consideração etiológica associada a fatores relacionais. Estranho como um conflito familiar pode se manifestar assim, não é? Patient: Sim, doutor. Obrigado por entender. Doctor: Vou orientar vocês a um psicólogo de casal para ajudarem a melhorar essa comunicação. Por enquanto, o que mais você sente com isso? Patient: Sinto muito envergonhado. E acho que a minha esposa também. Doctor: É natural. Vamos focar nisso. Certo, a consideração etiológica associada a fatores relacionais é o ponto principal do seu atendimento hoje. Continue tentando conversar com ela, e as coisas melhoram.

S: 68 বছর বয়সী পুরুষ রোগী বাম কোমরে এবং ফ্ল্যাঙ্কে হালকা থেকে মাঝারি ব্যথার অভিযোগ নিয়ে এসেছেন, যা গত ১ সপ্তাহ ধরে ১-২/১০ রেট করা হচ্ছে। তিনি অনিয়মিত প্রস্রাব, হেমাটুরিয়া বা সিসমেরিয়া অস্বীকার করেন। প্রস্রাবের আউটপুট স্বাভাবিক। তিনি হাইপারটেনশন এবং টাইপ ২ ডায়াবেটিসের রোগী। কোনো সাম্প্রতিক ইউরিনারি ট্র্যাক্ট ইনফেকশন বা আঘাতের ইতিহাস নেই।
O: ভাইটাল সাইন নর্মোস্ট্যাটিক। অ্যাবডোমিনাল এক্সাম: বাম উপরের চতুর্ভাগে মৃদু টেন্ডারনেস, ম্যাস বা পেরিটোনিয়াল সংকেত নেই। ডাইইউরেটিকের পর রেনাল আল্ট্রাসাউন্ড: বাম কিডনি স্বাভাবিক আকারের, ইকোটেক্সচার ঠিক আছে। তবে বাম ইউরেটারে ব্যাপক প্রসারণ এবং হাইড্রোনেফ্রোসিস দেখা যাচ্ছে। কোনো ইউরিনারি ক্যালকুলাস বা ইউরিনারি ট্র্যাক্ট ইনফেকশনের লক্ষণ নেই। ডিফারেনশিয়াল হিসেবে নেফ্রোপ্টোসিস, ইউরেটারাল কিঙ্কিং এবং রেনাল ইনফার্টেশন পুরোপুরি বাতিল (ruled out) করা হয়েছে।
A: বাম দিকে হাইড্রুয়ুরেটার।
P: ১. প্রস্রাব করার সময় প্রচুর পরিমাণে জল পান করতে পরামর্শ দেওয়া হয়েছে।
২. প্রস্রাব স্বাভাবিকভাবে বের হওয়ার জন্য পর্যবেক্ষণ করতে হবে।
৩. ২ সপ্তাহের মধ্যে ফলো-আপের জন্য নেফ্রোলজি বা ইউরোলজিতে রেফার করা হয়েছে।

Doctor: Hi, thanks for coming in. What brings you here today?
Patient: I feel like something is off with my sex life. I used to think about it all the time, but lately I don't really have any drive. My husband and I are starting to fight about it.
Doctor: Okay. Can you tell me if this has been going on for a while, or did it start recently? And is it every time you're intimate, or just sometimes?
Patient: I guess it's been a long time, maybe a year or two. It's pretty much always been like this since we got married, but we always just blamed it on stress. Honestly, we haven't really tried to have sex in a while because I just don't think about it.
Doctor: I see. And in the last six months, have you had any periods, or are you on any medications like antidepressants that could affect things?
Patient: I'm not on anything, and my periods are regular. No issues there.

We're going to rule out any medical causes first with some basic labs, but psychologically, this looks like a persistent low libido without a situational trigger.
Patient: So what exactly is wrong with me?

Doctor: I'll order some baseline labs to check your hormone levels, and then I'd like to refer you to a therapist who specializes in sex therapy to help you and your husband work through this. Doctor: That is really concerning, and I am sorry you are struggling with this. Based on what you have told me, it sounds like you developed this issue recently, not since childhood or adolescence. Given that you still reach climax during solo stimulation and this only seems to happen with your current partner, my main impression is that you have acquired situational anorgasmia. We can talk about adjusting your anxiety treatment or seeing a specialist to help with the stress if you'd like.
Patient: Okay. So you're saying I can still climax and it's just with him?
Doctor: Exactly. Since it is only occurring in this specific context and you have a history of normal function, we are looking at an acquired, situational issue. We will just work on managing the anxiety and see if that helps you return to your usual level of function.

S: 34-year-old male, C/O severe discomfort and inability to achieve vaginal penetration since the last 8 months. States the pain is sharp, localized, and worsens with attempted intercourse. Denies prior sexual dysfunction. No recent trauma, surgery, or infection. Asks for evaluation and possible treatment.

O: Vitals stable. Genitourinary exam within normal limits. No tenderness, lesions, or masses. Speculum exam deferred per patient preference.

P: Plan: (1) Reassured and educated that symptoms are manageable. (2) Scheduled follow-up with counselor for psychosexual therapy. (3) Medical management with topical 2% lidocaine prior to intercourse.

1. Sexual pain-penetration disorder, unspecified
2. Unrelated: Chronic tension-type headache (stable)

Patient: I'm 28 and I've been thinking for a while that I'm a woman living in a man's body. I can't keep up with the masculine side of things anymore; work is getting worse, and I don't want to be this person I look at in the mirror.

Doctor: So you're feeling that your gender identity doesn't match the sex you were assigned at birth. You mentioned you're feeling depressed and anxious about this. Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or ending things?

Patient: Yes, it gets really bad late at night when I'm alone. I feel trapped and I don't know how to get out.

Doctor: I hear how much pain you're in. It sounds like you want to transition and are struggling with the social and physical aspects of being perceived as a man.
Are you thinking about hormones or surgery right now, or are you just wanting help with the distress?

Patient: I want it all eventually. I can't stand having a beard or a deep voice. I want to shop in the women's clothing section. I want to be called by a different name and use she/her pronouns.

Doctor: Okay. The main thing I'm focused on right now is that gender incongruence of adulthood. We need to get you connected to a gender clinic for hormones and a referral, and I want to start you on an SSRI for the depressive symptoms while we figure out the next steps. I'm also going to refer you to a psychiatrist to talk through the safety plan and the suicidality.

Patient: I just want to feel normal and start living as myself.

Doctor: I understand, and we'll get you supported. Let's set up the psychiatric referral today and get the gender-affirming referral to a specialist clinic.

Doctor: Good afternoon. So, what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm really embarrassed to be here, doctor. I've never been able to achieve orgasm. I'm 29 years old and I'm in a relationship with a woman now, and I just... I don't think I've ever had one. I've only ever tried with my current partner, and I can't seem to climax during sex, even though I'm usually very turned on. I just get frustrated and it never happens. I was wondering if there's a physical problem or if I'm broken somehow.
Doctor: I appreciate you sharing that with me, and I want you to know that you are not broken. Let's talk about your history. You said you've never had an orgasm, correct?
Patient: Yes, never. I've only had sex with one person, my girlfriend, for about two years. I've touched myself before, but I've never actually reached the point where I could orgasm. The most stimulation I get is from clitoral rubbing during sex, and sometimes I feel like I'm close, but I just can't get over that edge.
Doctor: And when you are alone or masturbating, do you find that you can achieve orgasm?
Patient: No, I don't think I can. I've tried, but it never happens. It's always just me and my girlfriend. I don't know if I've ever been with anyone else, and I don't masturbate.
Doctor: Okay. And how about your physical health? Any surgeries, medications, or chronic conditions?
Patient: I'm generally healthy. I take birth control pills. No surgeries. No chronic diseases. I had a normal menstrual cycle growing up. No history of sexual trauma.
Doctor: Alright. I'm going to do a quick physical exam, just to make sure everything looks normal and there aren't any underlying physical issues.
Doctor: [exam findings noted: unremarkable pelvic exam, normal breast tissue, no signs of neurological deficit]
Patient: Is everything okay down there?
Doctor: Yes, everything appears completely normal and healthy. So, after reviewing everything, it sounds like you're dealing with a type of sexual dysfunction called anorgasmia. Specifically, because you've never been able to reach climax at any point in your life, it's classified as lifelong. And since it's only happening with your current partner and not, say, when you're alone or masturbating, we would call this situational. It's not a physical problem we can find on an exam; it's very common, and it sounds like there might be some psychological or relational factors at play, like anxiety around performance or just not knowing what your body responds to. I'd like to refer you to a sex therapist to help you explore self-pleasure and reduce the pressure during your intimate moments with your partner.
Patient: So I'm not broken?
Doctor: Not at all. We'll figure this out together.

S:
12 y/o F presents with chief complaint of 'not being able to use tampons and pain with intercourse.' Reports that she was never able to insert a tampon without severe pain and has never engaged in penetrative sexual activity. She can tolerate a speculum exam with minimal discomfort. Denies any history of sexual trauma. Denies dyspareunia with non-penetrative activities. Denies any painful medical procedures in the past. C-section for maternal reasons at birth, no other PMH.
O:
OB/GYN consult. On exam, vulva and vagina appear normal. Minimal discomfort with Q-tip touch at 12 o'clock but no significant guarding or provoked muscle spasm. No discharge, lesions, or atrophy. Speculum exam 90 mm with minimal external rotation. Cotton swab test negative.

A:
1. Lifelong situational sexual pain-penetration disorder (situational vaginismus).
2. Normal anatomy.

P:
1. Reassurance that diagnosis is benign and treatable. 
2. Referral to pelvic floor physical therapy to address conditioned muscle reaction to vaginal entry.
3. Discussed gradual desensitization using dilators at home, 5 min daily. 
4. F/u with OB/GYN in 6 weeks to assess tolerance with dilator use. 
5. No need for initial psychological therapy but open to referral if anxiety about exams increases.

Doctor: வணக்கம், சொல்லுங்க என்ன பிரச்சனை. Patient: வணக்கம் Doctor. நான் இப்போ ரெண்டாவது மாசத்துல இருக்கேன். Doctor: ஓ, சூப்பர். இந்த மாசம் எப்படி இருக்கு. Pain ஏதாவது இருக்கா. Pt presents with regular contractions 5 min apart x 3, ROM clear. 28+3 wks. GBS neg. Vaginal exam 2cm/70%, -show. Tocolytics held. NST reactive. Pt counseled on preterm labour. Admit for observation. Diagnosis: PTL.

S:
18 वर्षीय किशोर (Male) द्वारा पिछले 3 महीनों से संभोग के दौरान दर्द (dyspareunia) की शिकायत के साथ क्लिनिक में लाया गया। वह यौन रूप से सक्रिय (sexually active) है। मरीज ने बताया कि उसे संभोग के दौरान गहरा पेल्विक दर्द होता है जो काफी परेशान कर रहा है। कोई पूर्व यौन इतिहास (sexual history) नहीं है जिसमें दर्द का उल्लेख हो। मरीज कैजुअल सेक्स (casual sex) के दौरान दर्द की रिपोर्ट करता है, लेकिन यह समस्या अब सभी सेक्सुअल पार्टनर्स के साथ (generalised) हो गई है। मरीज ने बताया कि उसने अपनी पार्टनर को इस दर्द के बारे में पहले नहीं बताया था। कोई पूर्व यौन आघात (sexual trauma) या सर्जरी नहीं।

O:
A/E सामान्य है। वाइटल्स (Vitals) स्थिर: BP 120/80 mmHg, Pulse 72/min। पेल्विक (pelvic) और जेनिटल (genital) परीक्षा सामान्य। कोई इन्फेक्शन (infection), डिस्चार्ज (discharge) या पेरिनेल टेंडरनेस (perineal tenderness) नहीं। कोई न्यूरोलॉजिकल (neurological) या मस्कुलोस्केलेटल (musculoskeletal) समस्या नहीं।

A:
1. acquired generalised sexual pain-penetration disorder (पुरानी बीमारी / पुरानी कोई समस्या नहीं है, 3 महीने पहले शुरू हुई, अब generalised हो गई है)।
2. रूल्ड आउट (Ruled out): कोई ऑर्गेनिक कारण (organic cause) जैसे कि वल्वोडिनिया (vulvodynia) या पेल्विक इन्फ्लेमेटरी डिजीज (PID) नहीं है।

P:
1. सेक्सुअल काउंसलिंग (sexual counseling) और पेनिट्रेटिव सेक्स (penetrative sex) को अस्थायी रूप से रोकने (pause) की सलाह दी गई है।
2. फिजियोथेरेपी / पेल्विक फ्लोर फिजिओथेरेपी (pelvic floor physiotherapy) के लिए रेफरल (referral)।
3. फॉलो-अप (Follow-up) 2 सप्ताह में। अगर साइकोलॉजिकल/थेरेप्यूटिक कारणों से संबंधित हो तो बिहेवियरल थेरेपी (behavioral therapy) पर विचार किया जाएगा।

30M, G2P1, PTL 32w, presents to triage with contractions q4-5 min. Ob exam: 2 cm/50%/-3, ROM 2 hours ago. Fetal tracing category II. Patient requests vaginal delivery of 2nd twin. To delivery suite. Spontaneous labor 3 hrs. 1st twin vertex, Apgar 9/9, vaginal. 2nd twin in transverse lie, breech presentation. Failed external cephalic version. Emergent C-section for malpresentation. 2nd twin viable, Apgar 7/8, vaginal. Postpartum: stable. Discharge to home with 24h H&P. BP 110/70.

S:
Paciente feminina, 28 anos, G2P1, com gestação de 39+2 semanas, compareceu para acompanhamento ambulatorial de pré-natal. Relatou início há 4 horas de dores abdominais rítmicas com sangramento escuro, sem progressão. Apresentou taquicardia (FC 110 bpm) e hipertensão arterial (145/90 mmHg). Denunciou dor lombar e sensação de aperto no abdome. Nenhuma alteração neurológica ou do estado geral. Passado ginecologicamente 3+3/3-1. Nenhuma alteração no tempo de sangramento. No parto há 4 horas. Dores abdominais com sangramento, sem progressão. Cefálico, baio, com 40% de descida.

O:
Pressão arterial 145/90 mmHg; FC 110 bpm; SatO2 98% em ar ambiente; Temperatura 36,8 °C. Exame abdominal: útero firme e doloroso, com altissimos dores. Exame vaginal: sangramento escuro, 3+3/3-1. Cérvix: 2 cm dilatado, 70% efêmero, baio. Bebê: FC 150 bpm, com ausculta cardíaca regular, sem descompensação clínica da mãe. Sem evidências de descolamento placentário, prolapso de cordas, ou sangramento de alça. Sem meningismo, dor de cabeça, ou alteração do nível de consciência.

A:
1. Trabalho de parto com descompensação fetal não especificada. Apresenta taquicardia fetal (FC 150 bpm) e estresse fetal ao parto sem alteração mais específica do ritmo cardíaco, sem evidência de meconio amniótico ou alteração bioquímica documentada. Nível de estresse fetal moderado, com necesidad de monitorização contínua e eventual intervenção obstétrica se não houver melhora.
2. Hipertensão gestacional moderada. Acompanhamento ambulatorial com monitorização ambulatorial de pressão.

P:
- Acompanhamento ambulatorial urgente com monitorização fetal contínua pela via não invasiva. Considerar internação para monitorização cardiotocográfica contínua.
- Repouso em decúbito lateral esquerdo.
- Hidratação e controle da dor com paracetamol. Evitar analgésicos opioides até melhor definida a condição fetal.
- Repetir ecografia obstétrica se houver qualquer descompensação clínica da mãe ou do bebê.
- Manter-se em contato com a equipa de ginecologia de emergência para possível parto vaginal assistido ou parto por cesariana se a condição fetal persistir a descompensar. Semantizar a presença de cardiotocografia ambulatorial e de analgésicos opioides na prescrição.

34 yo G3P2, male identified, 16 wga presents with acute left calf swelling, redness, and tenderness. Homan's sign negative. Duplex confirms thrombosis of the left proximal deep calf veins. Doctor: নমস্কার, কী সমস্যা হয়েছে বলুন তো? Patient: নমস্কার ডাক্তারবাবু, আমার ডেলিভারির সময়টা চলছে। ডাক্তার: ও আচ্ছা, আপনি কত মাসের প্রেগন্যান্ট এখন? Patient: আট মাসের দু'সপ্তাহ আগে চলেছি। ডাক্তার: ঠিক আছে। লেবার কি শুরু হয়েছে? Patient: না, সকালে সূক্ষ্ম ব্যথা শুরু হয়েছিল, কিন্তু এখন কয়েক ঘণ্টা ধরে কোনো ব্যথা নেই। ডাক্তার: ব্লাড প্রেশার বা হার্ট রেট নিয়ে কোনো সমস্যা হচ্ছে কি? Patient: রাতে খুব ঠান্ডা লেগেছিল, একটু কাঁপুনি হচ্ছিল। ডাক্তার: ঠিক আছে, আমি চেক করে নিচ্ছি। আপনার কি বমি বমি ভাব বা মাথা ঘোরা আছে? Patient: না, শুধু সেই কাঁপুনিটা ছিল আর এখন হালকা জ্বর মনে হচ্ছে। ডাক্তার: বুঝতে পারছি। আপনি ডিহাইড্রেশনের কোনো লক্ষণ পাচ্ছেন কি? Patient: না, শুধু জ্বরটা আর কি। ডাক্তার: আমি চেক করলাম, আপনার ইউরিন টেস্টে ইনফেকশন দেখাচ্ছে না, ব্লাড প্রেশার নরমাল আছে, আর বেবি হার্ট রেটও একদম ঠিক আছে। ডাক্তার: আপনার শরীরে এই জ্বরটা এসেছে লেবার প্রসেস চলার সময়, যাকে আমরা Pyrexia during labour বলি। এটা খোঁজা খুব দরকার কারণ ডেলিভারির সময় এই জ্বরটা আসতে পারে। আপনি চিন্তা করবেন না, আমি আপনাকে অ্যান্টিবায়োটিক দিয়ে দিচ্ছি আর আপনার ভাইটালস মনিটর করছি। Patient: আচ্ছা, ধন্যবাদ ডাক্তারবাবু।

S: 32 y/o G1P0 female presents for routine 18-week anatomy and genetic screening. Obstetric history uncomplicated. No chronic medical conditions. The patient reports being in a monogamous relationship. She has received her first-trimester Combined Screening which was reported as screen-negative for trisomy 21, 18, and 13. She is requesting an NIPT as part of her prenatal workup and to discuss any additional testing. Her husband is available for counseling and is present in the room. She is employed as a high-school teacher and has no known family history of congenital anomalies or genetic disorders. She smokes occasionally on weekends. She denies any recent infections or exposure to teratogens. She reports feeling well and has had normal fetal movement.

O: Vitals: BP 118/72, HR 78, BMI 24.2. OB-Gyn exam: Fundal height 17cm, appropriate for dates. Fetal heart tones 152 bpm. No uterine irritability, no brown-red bleeding. No signs of preeclampsia or IUGR. Fetal biometry consistent with 18+4 weeks estimated gestational age. NIPT result: High-risk for trisomy 22 (Isochromosome 18p). Amniocentesis recommended for definitive diagnosis, with patient counseled on risks of procedure and loss rates. Result sent to maternal-fetal medicine as consult.

A: 1. Abnormal chromosomal finding on maternal antenatal screening (positive NIPT for isochromosome 18p / enlarged cell-free DNA in maternal circulation indicating trisomy 22 [cat-eye syndrome]).
2. Unscheduled aneuploidy screening positive.
3. Unspecified normal pregnancy.

P: Continue pregnancy with MFM follow-up. Schedule amniocentesis at 19-20 weeks. Counsel patient regarding risks of procedure, miscarriage, and the possibility of mosaicism. Provide written materials on cat-eye syndrome. If she declines invasive testing, offer fetal echocardiogram and detailed anatomy scan at 22 weeks. Repeat AFP and beta-hCG in 2 weeks. Avoid any medications with known fetal risks (Category X). Rebound appointment in 1 week to review counseling and schedule procedure. No prophylactic antibiotics or bed rest indicated. Ensure blood type and screen are current. Patient to weigh and monitor for signs of preterm labor or PPROM after procedure.

S: Mr. James P., 68y M, presents for routine gyn consult. He has a remote history of pelvic radiation for prostate cancer in 2005, now in remission. He reports chronic low-grade pelvic discomfort and occasional post-void dribbling. He has no current urinary retention, episodes of obstructed voiding, or hematuria. He denies any vaginal discharge, bleeding, or urinary tract infections. Socially, he lives independently. No planned pregnancies. Review of systems: constitutional negative; GU negative for pain, discharge, and hematuria. No skin lesions noted on external genitalia.

O: Vitals: BP 128/76, HR 72, Wt 88.4 kg. External inspection of the perineum reveals intact skin without fistulas. Speculum exam limited due to stenosis; unable to fully visualize the vaginal walls. A gentle white swab obtained for culture is negative. Urine dip negative.

Urine cultures, cervical cytology, and rectal exam performed in clinic today. Patient tolerates procedure well with minimal discomfort. No intra-abdominal masses palpable on rectovaginal exam.

A: 1. Vaginal stenosis secondary to past pelvic radiation / SUI-related pelvic organ support defect requiring evaluation for pelvic floor dysfunction / post-radiation changes.

2. BPH s/s (mild, stable).

P: 1. Discussed chronic pelvic radiation changes and vaginal stenosis with patient. Recommending topical estrogen 0.5 mg vaginally 3x/week for 3 months to improve mucosal resilience and comfort. Trial of oral estrogen 0.625 mg daily for 3 months to address urogenital atrophy and support pelvic tissue integrity. Will re-evaluate in 3 months.

2. Continue Flomax 0.4 mg daily and monitor BPH symptoms.

3. Pelvic floor PT referral for Kegel exercises and biofeedback to support lower pelvic support and improve continence.

4. UA, urine culture, and cytology sent today; will follow results in 7 days. Return sooner if hematuria, fever, or worsening pain occurs.
35F: dolor abdominal, sangrado vaginal. TCE+; ecografía sin HD, sin movimiento fetal. uterus size appropriate. HCG 1200. No se puede precisar época ni causa. Se ve al cardiólogo.

F 42 y/o pt presents with sudden high fevers, chills, and arthralgias ×2days. Travel hx: rural SE Asia 5mo ago. Hct 31, platelets 90K, LFTs elevated. Doctor: Hi, I have your results from the exam. The ultrasound shows a firm, rope-like band running down your daughter’s right neck, and the MRI confirms a thick, scarred sternocleidomastoid muscle that was probably torn during delivery. She has developed a tilted head posture and a small flattening on the right side of her skull. The right side of her face also looks a bit weaker, with the right eye drooping slightly. We need to start physical therapy right away and likely an orthotic collar to stretch the neck. We're also going to treat the facial nerve palsy with eye drops and refer you to a pediatric ophthalmologist to keep the cornea safe. Doctor: Good morning, Ms. R. Thank you for coming in today. I reviewed the ultrasound from your anatomy scan yesterday, and I wanted to go over the findings with you personally before we talk about next steps. Patient: Okay. Doctor: When the sonographer was looking at the baby’s anatomy, they paid special attention to the blood vessels in the umbilical cord. Patient: Everything looked okay? I thought the scan was fine. Doctor: The placenta is attached normally, and the baby appears otherwise healthy. However, the ultrasound showed that the umbilical cord has a slightly irregular shape or structural configuration. It’s not quite normal. Patient: What does that mean? Is it dangerous? Doctor: In some cases, the cord can have developmental differences in how the placental blood vessels connect. In your case, the cords anatomical pattern is different than expected. We will call this a structural developmental anomaly of the umbilical cord. Patient: Do you know exactly what the issue is? Like, is it a problem with the vessels or the length? Doctor: At this point, we do not have a specific label for the exact type of structural anomaly. We are not seeing an isolated single umbilical artery, and there are no clear cystic collections along the cord. We are simply seeing an irregular structural configuration of the cord itself. Therefore, we are classifying it as a structural developmental anomaly of the umbilical cord, unspecified. Patient: So what do we do now? Doctor: We will schedule a more detailed follow-up ultrasound in about two weeks to see if the configuration remains stable or changes as the pregnancy progresses. We will also perform a fetal echocardiogram to ensure the baby’s heart is developing normally regardless of the cord shape. In the meantime, we will monitor your standard prenatal screenings closely. If you have any bleeding, a sudden decrease in fetal movement, or leaking fluid before your next appointment, call us immediately.

Doctor: Bonjour, asseyez-vous. Je vois que vous avez une consultation pour un bilan. Comment allez-vous aujourd'hui ?
Patient: Bonjour. Ça va, il y a juste ces douleurs et ces bleus qui apparaissent tout le temps. Ça m'inquiète un peu.
Doctor: C'est normal de s'inquiéter. Pouvez-vous me raconter quand tout a commencé et de quoi vous vous plaignez exactement ?
Patient: J'avais environ 12 ans, je me suis tordu la cheville en cours de sport. L'articulation était hypermobile, mais ça a guéri. Depuis, j'ai des douleurs chroniques dans les genoux, les coudes et le dos. Je me fais souvent des bleus pour un rien, même sans me prendre un coup. Ma peau aussi est très fine, elle s'étale et fait des cicatrices en forme de clous de girofle.
Doctor: Ça me semble assez spécifique, surtout la répartition des bleus et la texture de votre peau. Vous avez déjà eu des tests génétiques pour vérifier si vous aviez un syndrome des tissus conjonctifs ?
Patient: Non, c'est la première fois. J'ai vu un kiné, mais ça ne suffit plus.
Doctor: D'accord. Je vais vous examiner maintenant. [Examen cliniques] Je vois une hyperlaxité articulaire diffuse, pas seulement à un niveau, et une peau hyperextensible. Ces constatations sont très évocatrices.
Doctor: Je pense que vous souffrez de syndrome d'Ehlers-Danlos classique. Ce n'est pas un syndrome indéterminé, c'est bien cette forme spécifique avec les bleus et les cicatrices caractéristiques.
Patient: C'est une forme rare ? Qu'est-ce que ça change pour moi ?
Doctor: Ça change le suivi, car cette forme est plus liées aux complications articulaires et cutanées. On va vous orienter vers un service spécialisé pour un bilan génétique et un plan de prise en charge adapté.

Doctor: So you're here because your mom noticed something on your chest X-ray, right? Can you tell me a bit about what happened?  
Patient: Yeah, well, I had a physical for soccer last month and they did the chest film. I didn't have any pain or anything, I just had to see what the doctor thought about it.  
Doctor: I see. And you haven't had any recent chest trauma, right? No rib fractures?  
Patient: No, I've never broken a rib.  
Doctor: Okay. And you don't have any issues with your arm strength or chest wall movement?  
Patient: No, I'm totally fine. I play basketball so I need my strength.  
Doctor: I looked through the radiologist's report. It sounds like a pretty harmless incidental finding. On the left side, you have a bifid rib—meaning one of the upper ribs is split into two separate bony segments that both attach to the spine and the sternum. It's a congenital thing, a developmental quirk in how that rib formed when you were growing. It's not a fracture, it's not an extra floating rib, and it's not affecting your muscles or blood vessels like you'd see in something like Poland syndrome.  
Patient: Oh, okay. So do I need to do anything about it?  
Doctor: No, you're fine. No surgery or bracing needed. It's stable, it's not going to cause you any problems, and it's not going to affect your growth or your activities. Just leave it alone and keep playing basketball. If anything changes, let us know. Does that make sense to you?  
Patient: Yeah, totally.  
Doctor: Great. I'll put that in your chart. Try to have a good rest of your day.

Doctor: Good afternoon. I have the imaging results back. We did the renal ultrasound and the repeat doppler to check on your left kidney since you had that flank pain. The left kidney is completely absent. It’s a congenital issue—you were born without the left kidney. This is called renal agenesis, which is why it hasn't been growing or causing the pain. We’ll just keep monitoring your right kidney function with urine tests and bloodwork every three months. Stay well hydrated. Are you feeling okay with this plan?

Patient: Oh, so I only have one kidney? Is that why it keeps hurting?

Doctor: Exactly. Since you have only one kidney, it's working overtime and some people get a dull ache. We'll watch your creatinine levels and your blood pressure. If the pain gets sharp or you get a fever, call us right away. We also want to make sure you don't have any urinary tract infections since you only have one kidney to protect you. ডাক্তার: আজকে তোমাকে কেন নিয়ে আসছ তারা? কী হয়েছে? 
রোগী: গত এক ঘণ্টা ধরে বুকটা খুব ব্যথা করছে, আর মনে হচ্ছে শ্বাস নিতে খুব কষ্ট হচ্ছে। মুখ দিয়ে জোরে জোরে শ্বাস নিচ্ছি। হাত-পা অবশ অবশ লাগছে। 
ডাক্তার: বুঝতে পারছি। তুমি ঘাবড়ে যেও না। শ্বাস নেওয়ার গতিটা একটু কমে দাও, ধীরে ধীরে শ্বাস নাও, আর নাক দিয়ে ছাড়ো। তোমার হাত-পা কি ঠাণ্ডা হয়ে যাচ্ছে বা ঝিনঝিন করছে? 
রোগী: হ্যাঁ, হাত-পা একদম বরফের মতো ঠান্ডা মনে হচ্ছে, আর আঙুলগুলো একটু কুঁচকে যাচ্ছে। 
ডাক্তার: ঠিক আছে, এটা 'হাইপারভেন্টিলেশন'-এর কারণে হচ্ছে। তুমি আগের মতো জোরে জোরে শ্বাস নিলে শরীরে কার্বন ডাইঅক্সাইডের মাত্রা কমে যায়, যার জন্য রক্তনালী সংকুচিত হয়ে হাত-পা অবশ লাগে আর বুক ভারী লাগে। এটা ভয়ের কিছু নয়, মাত্র শ্বাস-প্রশ্বাসের গতিটা একটু কমিয়ে দাও। এটা কি কোনো স্ট্রেস বা ভয়ের কারণে হচ্ছে, নাকি খুব রেস করে দৌড়ানোর পর হয়েছে? 
রোগী: স্ট্রেসের কারণে হচ্ছে, একটু আগে খুব জোরে জোরে শ্বাস নিচ্ছিলাম। 
ডাক্তার: বুঝতে পেরেছি। এখন থেকে যখনই এমন হবে, একটা কাগজের ব্যাগ বা নিজের হাতের তালু দিয়ে মুখটা ঢেকে রাখো এবং স্বাভাবিকভাবে শ্বাস নাও। এতে কার্বন ডাইঅক্সাইড আবার শরীরে ফিরে আসবে। আর যদি বারবার এমন হয়, তাহলে একবার চেকআপ করিয়ে নিও। এখন তুমি একটু শান্ত হয়ে বসো, সব ঠিক হয়ে যাবে।

Patient:   হ্যাঁ ডাক্তারবাবু, গত কয়েক সপ্তাহ ধরে আমার একটু সমস্যা হচ্ছে। আমি যখন ফোনে কথা বলি, বা বাড়িতে বসে খবরের কাগজ পড়ি, তখন মনে হয় শব্দের অর্থ গায়েব হয়ে যাচ্ছে। আমি জানি অক্ষরগুলো কী, কিন্তু সেগুলো কোনো অর্থ তৈরি করছে না।

Doctor:   আচ্ছা, আপনি কি অন্য ভাষায় কথা বললে বা অন্য কাউকে বললে এই একই সমস্যা হয়? মানে, শুধু বাংলা পড়ার সময়, নাকি ইংরেজি বা অন্য কিছু পড়লেও হয়?

Patient:   বাংলাতেই বেশি হয়। ইংরেজি বা হিন্দি খবর পড়লেও তেমন হয় না, বা অনেক কম হয়।

Doctor:   বুঝতে পারছি। আপনি কি আগের মতো কাজ করছেন? মানে, আপনার অফিসে কোনো হিসাব বা খাতা-কলমের কাজ করতে গিয়ে কোনো অসুবিধা হচ্ছে না তো? আপনি তো নিজেই হিসাবপত্র সামলান, তাই না?

Patient:   হ্যাঁ হ্যাঁ, অফিসে কোনো সমস্যা নেই। আমি সব ঠিকঠাক সামলে নিচ্ছি। কিন্তু বাড়িতে বসে যখন বই বা খবরের কাগজ পড়ি, তখন শব্দের সাথে অর্থ আর মিলতে চায় না।

Doctor:   লিখতে বা বানান করতে কোনো সমস্যা হচ্ছে, আপনার স্ত্রীর মতে? আপনি কি যা বলতে চান তা লিখে রাখতে পারেন?

Patient:   লেখালেখির কাজও ঠিকঠাকই করছি। স্ত্রীর সাথে ফোনে কথা বলি, সব স্বাভাবিক। শুধু পড়ার সময় এই অদ্ভুত সমস্যাটা হয়, যেখানে মনে হয় পড়া শব্দগুলো আর কোনো অর্থ তৈরি করছে না।

Doctor:   আপনার কথা শুনে মনে হচ্ছে আপনার কোনো প্রতীকী কার্যকারিতার ব্যাঘাত ঘটেছে। যেহেতু আপনি সাধারণ লেখা বা হিসাবের কাজ করতে পারছেন না, আর শুধু পড়ার সময় এই বিচ্ছিন্ন সমস্যাটা হচ্ছে, তাই আমি এটাকে নির্দিষ্ট কোনো ডিসলেক্সিয়া বা অন্য কোনো সুনির্দিষ্ট সমস্যা হিসেবে দেখছি না। আপনার সাময়িকভাবে কোনো বাস্পীয় বা মানসিক কারণ আছে কি, যা সম্প্রতি বদলেছে?

Patient:   না, আমি খুব একটা মানসিক চাপ নিই না। আমি রাতে ঠিকমতো ঘুমিয়েছি, খাওয়া-দাওয়ায় কোনো পরিবর্তন নেই।

Doctor:   বুঝলাম। আপনার চোখ বা কান পরীক্ষা করে দেখা হয়েছে তো? চোখের পাওয়ার বা কানের কোনো সমস্যা নেই তো?

Patient:   না, চোখের ডাক্তারবাবু গত মাসে পরীক্ষা করে বলেছেন দৃষ্টি একদম ঠিক আছে। কানের পরীক্ষাও গত বছর করা হয়েছিল, সব নরমাল।

Doctor:   ঠিক আছে, তাহলে আমাদের ধরে রাখতে হবে যে আপনার একটি প্রতীকী কার্যকারিতার ব্যাঘাত বা symbolic dysfunction রয়েছে। আমি নিশ্চিত করছি, যেহেতু আপনার কোনো সুনির্দিষ্ট টাইপিং বা পড়ার সমস্যা, হিসাব বা লিখিত ভাষার ব্যত্যয় হচ্ছে না, তাই এটা একটি **unspecified symbolic dysfunction** বা অনির্দিষ্ট প্রতীকী কার্যকারিতার ব্যাধি। আমি আপনাকে কিছু মানসিক পরীক্ষা এবং আগামী সপ্তাহে আবার দেখাতে বলব। আপাতত কোনো প্রেসক্রিপশন দেওয়া হচ্ছে না।

Doctor: Alright, Mrs. Carter, I've got your recent urine culture results back from Dr. Chen’s lab. The bacteria in your urine are actually quite resistant. The lab says it's a type of Enterobacterales, and it is one that does not respond to third-generation cephalosporin drugs like ceftriaxone. They did the extended spectrum beta-lactamase testing, and it is positive, but the bug is not producing carbapenemase enzymes, so it is not resistant to carbapenem antibiotics. The organism is also not susceptible to fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, though it is still susceptible to nitrofurantoin. It's a very common gut bacteria, and it is causing a symptomatic UTI. We are going to put you on nitrofurantoin for ten days. Please make sure you finish the full course and stay well-hydrated. I also need to check if you are allergic to any medications before we fill this prescription.

Patient: Is it serious? I was on an antibiotic last week, something like Zithromax or a similar one?

Doctor: Because you had taken a third-generation cephalosporin recently, it likely cleared out the good bacteria in your gut and allowed this resistant strain to overgrow and cause the infection. It's not a carbapenem-resistant organism, which is a much more concerning scenario, but we do need to treat it properly with a different class of drugs. I'll schedule a follow-up test in two weeks to make sure your urine is completely clear. Does that sound okay to you?

Patient: Yes, I'll take the nitrofurantoin. Thank you.

Doctor: You're welcome. Just call us if you develop a fever, chills, or if your back starts hurting.

S: Enfant F, 5 ans, présentée pour consultation suite à une prise de substance toxique non identifiée. Passé médical de base sans antécédent notable. La maman rapporte que l'enfant a été découverte en train de mâcher des baies d'un arbuste dans le jardin. L'enfant présentait des vomissements, une hypersalivation et une léthargie. Pas de fièvre, pas de douleur abdominale localisée. L'enfant ne peut pas communiquer l'ingestion précise. Phosphomolybdique administré par le 159 en route.

O: Vitals stables. Température: 36.8°C. Taux cardiaque: 110/min. Pression artérielle: 95/55 mmHg. Éveil obnubilé (Glasgow 13/15). Pupilles isocore et réactives. Pas de signs cutanés spécifiques.

A: Toxicose non précisée: Enfant avec intoxication par ingestion de substance végétale non identifiée. Pas d'antécédents de maladies chroniques significatifs. Pas d'autres toxiques évidents (médicaments, produits de nettoyage). Pas d'atteinte hépatique ni néphrologique à ce stade.

P: Continue la surveillance en pédiatrie. Surveillance des paramètres biologiques (CPK, bilan hépatique, créatininémie). Maintenir NPO et IV. Drainage urinaire. Retrait de la substance (maman doit amener un échantillon de la plante). Pas d'antidote spécifique identifié. Sortie à envisager si l'évolution est favorable sous 24h.

Patient: Hello, Doctor. I’ve been having this discharge lately. That’s why I came.

Patient: About three weeks ago, just a normal discharge. But recently, it’s changed. It’s more like a thick, yellow stuff, like cottage cheese.

Doctor: Okay. Any itching or burning with that?

Doctor: Any abnormal odor?

Doctor: I see. Let me do an exam. Hmm. The cervix looks normal. I’m going to take a swab from the vagina to check for the exact cause.

Patient: Okay.

Doctor: Based on what you described, the thick white discharge and the itching, I’m pretty sure this is a yeast infection. We’ll send the swab to confirm, but I’m starting you on an antifungal cream right away. Try not to put any soap down there and wear cotton underwear. We’ll check back to make sure it clears up.

S: ३८ वर्षीय महिला सलग ४ महिन्यांपासून उजव्या खालच्या जबड्यामध्ये (mandible) तीव्र, ठणठणीत (throbbing) वेदना होत असल्याची तक्रार करत आहे. या वेदनांमुळे तिला रात्री झोप येत नाही आणि कामावर लक्ष केंद्रित करणे कठीण जात आहे. परंपरेने डेंटल क्लिनिकमध्ये रूट कॅनाल (root canal) आणि एक्स-रे (X-ray) केले गेले. आजूबाजूला कोणतीही सूज (swelling) नाही, ताप नाही. ती सध्या कोणतेही औषध घेत नाही.

O: तपासणीमध्ये उजव्या बाजूचा दाढ (molar region) दागाळलेला दिसतो. दाढावर उघडा कॅविटी (cavity) आहे. पेरियोडोंटल प्रोबिंग (periodontal probing) सामान्य मर्यादेत आहे. जबड्याचे हालचाल (TMJ movement) मर्यादित नाही. सायनस (sinus) मध्ये कोणतीही लक्षणे नाहीत.

A: १. क्रॉनिक डेंटल पेन (Chronic dental pain) - उजवीकडील कॅरीज (caries) आणि अनेक वर्षांचा दुर्लक्षित उपचार यामुळे.
२. क्रॉनिक सेकंडरी ऑरोफेशियल पेन (Chronic secondary orofacial pain) - याला वेगळे ठरवणारा घटक म्हणजे खालच्या दाढामध्ये दिसलेला कॅरीज, ज्यामुळे बॅक्टेरियल इन्फेक्शन वाढून थेट दाढामध्ये वेदना होत आहेत.

P: १. दाढाची तातडीची रिस्टोरेटिव्ह ट्रीटमेंट (restorative treatment) आणि रूट कॅनाल (RCT) प्लॅन केली आहे. पेन नीडल (local anesthesia) देऊन कॅरीज हटवून दाढा भरणे.
२. कॅल्सियम हायड्रॉक्साईड (calcium hydroxide) आणि लेडोकॅन (lignocaine) इंजेक्शन्स देऊन आताच तात्पुरती ट्रॉमा ( Trauma) कमी करण्यासाठी लोकल ॲनेस्थेशिया दिला.
३. ३ दिवसांनी फॉलो-अप (follow-up) आणि पेनकिलर्स (NSAID) सुरू करण्याचा सल्ला.
४. तोंडाची स्वच्छता (oral hygiene) सुधारण्यासाठी सूचना.

S: 17 y/o F presents for evaluation of a facial burn. Patient states she was applying self-tanner at home 2 days ago when she accidentally bumped the bottle into the pot of hot wax on her stovetop; the liquid splashed onto her right cheek and perioral area. She states pain was immediate, with subsequent swelling and blistering. Denies any vision changes or ocular symptoms. No other burns on exam. Past hx: mild asthma, last treated with albuterol PRN at age 12.

O: Vitals: T 36.8C, HR 78, BP 110/70, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA. General: Alert, in mild distress. Exam of face: erythematous, edematous skin involving approximately 15% of right cheek and extending to the lower chin. Multiple small, flaccid bullae present, some with intact roofs, others partially de-roofed revealing a moist, pink, bleeding base. Pain is 3/10. No involvement of eyelids, eyebrows, or periorbital skin. Pupil equal, reactive; no corneal findings. No other burns noted on head, neck, trunk, or extremities. Skin turgor normal; no signs of dehydration.

A: 1. Superficial partial thickness facial burn, right cheek and chin, thermal. 2. Mild localized edema/erythema. 3. Asthma, intermittent (stable).

P: 1. Wound care: Gentle cleansing with saline, apply topical silver sulfadiazine 1% cream to burns daily; keep area covered with non-adherent gauze. 2. Pain control: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q6h PRN pain; acetaminophen 500 mg PO q6h PRN. 3. Tetanus: Ensure Tdap is up to date; give Td if >10 years since last. 4. Follow-up: Return to clinic in 3 days or sooner if increased pain, purulence, or vision changes. 5. Patient education on burn healing, infection signs, and return precautions. 6. Dermatology referral as needed in 2 weeks for scar prevention.

Reports sudden sharp pain in anterior right hip, unable to continue running, now has significant pain with ambulation and inability to actively flex hip past 70 degrees. Denies any fall, direct blow, or previous hip injury. Denies paresthesias, numbness, or weakness in the leg. Denies bowel/bladder dysfunction. No sick contacts.

O: Vitals vital signs stable. Inspects right hip shows no ecchymosis, deformity, or laceration. Palpation is most tender over right iliopsoas tendon insertion at lesser trochanter and along the right groin musculature. Active hip flexion and internal rotation are painful with guarding. Negative straight leg raises, negative Faber, and negative log roll. Neurovascular exam intact: 5/5 strength in all major muscle groups distally, capillary refill <2 seconds, sensation intact to light touch and pinprick in dermatomal distribution. No hip joint effusion or warmth.

A: Acute strain of right hip flexor musculotendinous unit, most likely involving the iliopsoas tendon and surrounding fascia. No evidence of laceration, open wound, or significant traumatic hematoma. Differential considered and ruled out: hip joint dislocation, lumbar radiculopathy, and avulsion fracture (negative x-rays).

P: Rest, ice, compression, and elevation. Prescribe NSAIDs (ibuprofen 600 mg PO q6h PRN). Advise relative rest, avoid aggravating activities, and physical therapy referral to initiate gentle range of motion and eccentric strengthening this week. Reevaluate in 7-10 days or sooner if worsening pain, inability to bear weight, or new neurologic deficits develop.

RNP. Homem 36 anos, colisão frontal MV. Trauma facial. Rinoscopia com sigmoidoscopia nasal: amputação traumática de nariz completa (extremidade distal não identificada). S: পুরুষ, ২৮ বছরsterile। গত ৩ দিন আগে ডান চোখে ঘন ঘন আঘাত লেগেছে বলে জানাচ্ছে, যার ফলে চোখের চারপাশে ব্যথা ও দৃষ্টিতে সামান্য ঝাপসা ভাব হচ্ছে। রোগী জানান যে চোখে স্পষ্টভাবে কোনো পাথর বা কাঁচের টুকরো প্রবেশ করেনি।

O: সজাগ ও স্থির। ডান চোখের সামনের দিকে হালকা পারিপার্শ্বিক এদিমা (periorbital edema) সহ সামান্য রক্তজমাট বাঁধা (subconjunctival hemorrhage) দেখা যাচ্ছে। কর্নিয়া খাঁজ কাটা বা ছিদ্র হওয়ার কোনো প্রমাণ নেই। চোখের মণি স্বাভাবিক আকারের এবং আলোতে সমানভাবে সংকুচিত হচ্ছে। ফান্ডোস্কোপি (Fundoscopy) স্বাভাবিক। চোখের চাপ (IOP) এবং আলোতে সংকুচিত হওয়ার হার (RAPD) স্বাভাবিক।

A: চোখে আঘাত (Eye trauma)।

P: টিস্যুর আঘাতের সাথে সম্পর্কিত ব্যথা নিরাময়ের জন্য প্যারাসিটামল (Paracetamol) ৫০০ মি.গ্রা., দিনে ৩ বার খাওয়ার পরামর্শ দেওয়া হয়েছে। চোখে কোনো মলম বা ড্রপ প্রয়োগ করার প্রয়োজন নেই। রোগী চোখে হাত না দেওয়ার এবং ২৪ ঘণ্টা বিশ্রাম নেওয়ার নির্দেশ দিয়েছেন। চোখে কোনো চাপ না দিয়ে ২ সপ্তাহে ফলো-আপ (follow-up) করতে বলা হয়েছে।

আনুষঙ্গিক: হাইপারটেনশন (Hypertension) - স্থিতিশীল।

Doctor: नमस्कार. काय झालं? तोंडात कसं दुखावलं गेलं? 3 दिवसांपूर्वी सायकल चालवताना खाली पडलो, वाकून सायकल उचलत होतो तेव्हा ओंढणी खाली पडली. तेव्हापासून डाव्या जबड्याच्या खालच्या भागात लय वेदना आहेत आणि काहीतरी तुटल्यासारखं वाटतंय. तोंड उघडायला पण त्रास होतोय. ओंठ बघूया... इथे डावीकडे खालच्या जबड्याच्या कोपऱ्याला (mandible च्या angle ला) एक छोटीशी जखम दिसतेय, आतून रक्ताची खळगी लागली आहे आणि सूज पण आहे. मान थोडी कडक झाली आहे. ओंठ हलवून बघ... हो, इथं हाडाचा टोकदार भाग आहे, म्हणजे खालचा जबडा (mandible) तिथून तुटला आहे. आपण एक एक्स-रे काढून बघूया, पण असं दिसतंय की ही जबड्याच्या खालच्या हाडाची (angle of mandible) फ्रॅक्चर आहे, कंडाइलची किंवा दाढ लागण्याची जागा तुटलेली नाहीये. आजपासून सॉलिड जेवण बंद आणि फक्त लिक्विड घ्या. मी तुम्हाला अँटीबायोटिक्स आणि वेदनाशामक औषध लिहून देतो. उद्या हाडजोड तज्ज्ञाकडे (maxillofacial) घेऊन जा, ते प्लास्टर किंवा वायर लावतील. आणखी काही त्रास जाणवला तर सांगा.

Rm. 45M. Apresenta-se após escalada mecânica nao-transporte. C/F 15m. TCS 'Negativo'. DRE cervical sem alteracao neurológica. DV/DO 'Normal'. Rx cervical/dorsal 'Nao achado'. ATX 'Nao aplicável'. Aconselhamento. Acompanhamento na 1ª निचले semana.

S: 5-year-old male brought by mother for urgent ED referral regarding a lower abdominal/groin area burn. Mother states patient slipped and fell onto the corner of a metal radiator while playing. A: 1. Full thickness burn of the perineum and genitalia - located on the left labial/scrotal junction and inner thigh, approximately 2x3 cm, deep partial/full thickness appearance with eschar and clear demarcation. 2. Abdominal wall abrasion with minimal erythema - secondary mechanism. 3. Anxiety/pain secondary to burn.
O: Vitals: T 36.8, HR 110, RR 24, BP 95/55, O2 sat 99% RA. Exam: Well-appearing, alert, and crying. Skin: Deep, well-demarcated, white to tan, leathery burn with no blisters, no capillary refill, no sensation to light touch on the affected area. Surrounding tissue appears edematous. No signs of circumferential burn. 2+ peripheral pulses. No distal edema. Neurovascular status of lower extremities is intact. Urethral meatus is not involved, no urine staining noted on undergarments. Wound is clean, dry, and non-perfused.
P: 1. Immediate referral to Pediatric Burn Center for possible escharotomy, grafting, and pain management. 2. Tetanus status updated. 3. Pain control with IV morphine titrated for comfort. 4. NPO status maintained.
F/U: Follow up at Burn Center within 1 hour.

Doctor: Bonjour Alexandre, je vais revoir votre dossier et mécanisme du traumatisme créanien. Vous méniez un accident de ski la semaine dernière, un choc frontal contre un portique suite à une chute. Vous avez eu une aménée délibérée pour scanner et angiographie. Patient: Oui, c'est bien comme je vous l'ai dit. J'ai eu la tâte qui a heurté le poteau, j'ai perdu connaissance un instant, puis des nausées et une forte migraine. J'ai eu une petite aménée en urgence le lendemain car je vomissais. Je n'ai pas perdu de temps. Patient: J'ai continué découvert ce matin un ecchymose sur le cuir chevelu, mais je ne me suis pas cogné le cou. J'ai eu des vertiges et des flashs visuels pendant deux jours, mais pas de douleur nasale ou faciale. Patient: J'ai bien repris une alimentation normale, je n'ai pas eu de vomissements de sang ni de saignements de nez. Je n'ai pas pris de anticoagulants non plus. Doctor: J'ai reçu votre IRM. On y voit une dissection de l'artère vertèbrale gauche au niveau C3-C4 sans extension intracréanienne et sans signe d'embolie. Le scanner en coupe fine a fait le point. Patient: C'est la principale blessure je suppose ? Doctor: Oui. Votre atteinte est limitée à l'artère vertébrale gauche, une dissection artérielle, à l'intracréanien. C'est une blessure des vaisseaux sanguins du créne, intra-cranienne. On n'a rien vu au niveau des artères carotides ni des veines éxtracréaniennes de la face et du cou. Le scanner ne montrait pas de fracture du crâne ni de saignements à l'extérieur. Patient: Et la suite, je dois faire attention à la circulation sanguine ? Doctor: On garde une surveillance neurologique. On vous mettra sous antiagrégent plaquettaire, aspirin 100 mg, pendant trois mois maximum. Vous ne retrouverez pas le ski avant six semaines minimum, et on surveillera l'amélioration de vos vertiges. Patient: Très bien, je comprends. J'ai bien eu le choc frontal sur la tête, et la douleur a transité par la base du crâne. Je dois rapporter tout symptôme nouveau à l'urgence. Doctor: Exact. On garde un suivi en neurologue. Je vais noter votre diagnostic principal comme une blessure des vaisseaux sanguins du crâne, localisation intra-cranienne, artère vertébrale gauche. Ne vous inquiétez pas, les pronostics sont bons si on surveille bien le risque embolique.

S: Patient is a 17-year-old male presenting with his mother for a routine urology consult. Mother reports the patient has a known history of cryptorchidism status post left orchiopexy. Today he is here to discuss family planning options and potential reproductive health implications of his past diagnosis. He declines discussing sexual history and no sexual activity is reported. He has no dysuria, hematuria, or pelvic pain. No discharge noted.

O: Vitals stable. Abdominal exam benign. Genital exam shows normally developed penis, inguinal rings intact, both testes descended and palpable. No masses, varicocele, or hydrocele appreciated.

U/A/A: No evidence of urolithiasis, infection, or malignancy on current workup. Discussed reproductive implications of cryptorchidism and offered referral to the fertility services liaison for counseling regarding future family building options. Pt is a 62 y/o male referred for second opinion re: surgical vs radiation management of a prior malignancy. O: Vitals WNL, chest clear to auscultation, no masses appreciated. Labs: Hgb 12.8, WBC 6.5, Plt 240K. Plan: Continue routine surveillance with annual CT scan. Continue low-dose aspirin for cardiovascular prophylaxis as discussed in prior visit. S: 42 y/o M presents with history of being caught in an industrial blast approximately 20 hours ago. Pt states he was standing near a heavy machinery unit when an unexpected detonation occurred. He reports generalized anxiety, headache, and non-specific chest discomfort but denies LOC, auditory or visual changes, or external burns. A: 1. Blast exposure, unspecified. 2. Anxiety related to traumatic event. Rule out pneumothorax, tympanic membrane rupture, and traumatic stress reaction, though physical exam and initial imaging findings (CXR, e-FAST) are negative for acute pathology.

P: 1. Continue routine observation and serial monitoring for delayed complications. 2. Cardiology clearance given hx of CAD and chest discomfort; EKG and troponins sent, expected to be negative based on bedside assessment. 3. Benzodiazepine PRN for acute agitation/anxiety. 4. Trauma registry and occupational safety reporting. 5. Patient educated on expected recovery trajectory and instructed to return to ED immediately for worsening chest pain, dyspnea, or neurological symptoms. 6. PCP follow-up in 1 week.

**S:** 8-year-old male patient brought to the outpatient clinic by his mother for follow-up and cognitive screening. States he was crossing the local train tracks to get to the park when a stationary maintenance train unexpectedly rolled downhill and struck his left leg. The patient was not run over by the locomotive; instead, the flatbed car bumped into his left lower extremity. He reports localized pain, swelling, and a visible contusion over the lateral malleolus, but no open fracture or deformity. He was taken to the ED initially but was discharged home with analgesia and follow-up. Mother states the incident was unintentional; the boy lost his footing near the rails and was struck. No other victims or collisions were involved.

**O:** Vitals stable. General: Alert, cooperative. Cardiovascular and respiratory exam unremarkable. Musculoskeletal: Left lateral leg swelling and ecchymosis over the lateral malleolus, approximately 8x10 cm. No point tenderness over the tibial shaft or calcaneus. Range of motion of the left ankle is painful but nearly full (0–15 degrees dorsiflexion, 0–30 degrees plantarflexion). No lacerations or exposed bone. Neurovascular: Capillary refill <2 seconds, palpable dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses. Sensation intact to light touch in the left foot. Full strength on manual muscle testing 4/5.

**A:**
1. Railway transport injury event of undetermined intent without collision or derailment (ICD-10-CM: V93.2)
   - Traumatic blunt force injury sustained when patient was struck by a swerving railway car while trespassing on the tracks. Intent remains undetermined pending review of the site and patient safety assessment.
2. Contusion, left lateral ankle, uncomplicated
   - Post-traumatic soft tissue injury, managed expectantly.

**P:**
- Ice, elevation, and compression wrap for left ankle contusion for 48 hours.
- Strict non-weight-bearing for 72 hours; prescribe crutches and follow up with ortho if pain limits ambulation.
- Neurovascular checks of the left foot every 2 hours while awake.
- Pain management: Recommend alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen PRN; avoid aspirin.
- Refer to social work for evaluation of rail yard access and patient safety planning.
- Re-evaluate in 3 days in the orthopedic clinic.

S: 52 y/o male presents today for outpatient evaluation and travel vaccination counseling. He is planning to relocate to rural northeastern Brazil for a 12-month humanitarian mission in 4 weeks. He reports no prior vaccinations against leishmaniasis, growth, or hepatitis A/B. He denies any recent insect bites, pet exposure, or abnormal skin lesions. He has a history of hypertension well-controlled with lisinopril 10 mg daily.

O: Vitals: BP 128/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm. General: Alert and well-developed, in no acute distress. Skin: No open sores, ulcers, or papules; no signs of cutaneous leishmaniasis. He denies lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or cachexia.

Lab/Imaging: CBC, CMP, HIV screen, and tetanus titers sent today.

Assessment: A. Leishmaniasis prophylaxis and travel medicine consult for upcoming deployment to endemic region. B. HTN. C. Unrelated: Seasonal allergic rhinitis.

P: 1. Discussed that leishmaniasis is a parasitic infection transmitted by sandfly vectors endemic in tropical regions including Brazil. He will be working in outdoor/rural areas at high risk. 
2. Administered first dose of liposomal amphotericin-B intramuscular injection as pre-exposure prophylaxis for leishmaniasis (VCL-HB01). Second dose scheduled in 6 weeks prior to departure. 
3. Counselled on protective measures: DEET-based insect repellent, permethrin-treated clothing, and bed netting. 
4. Order CBC, CMP, HIV screening, and tetanus titers for travel clearance. 
5. Follow up in 30 days to review labs and administer second dose of anti-leishmaniasis immunization.

S: 42 y/o male presents for outpatient evaluation of persistent symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection approximately 8 months ago. Initial infection was uncomplicated, managed at home with supportive care. Since recovery, he has experienced daily fatigue described as 'brain fog' and exertional dyspnea that limits him to 2 flights of stairs. He also reports persistent intermittent headaches and mild post-exertional malaise (PEM) where symptoms worsen 24-48 hours after physical or cognitive exertion. He has developed new-onset varicose veins and occasional periorbital edema. Denies fever, productive cough, or acute chest pain. He has tried over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen with minimal relief. No prior psychiatric diagnosis. Background: mild seasonal allergic rhinitis.

O: Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 78, RR 16, SpO2 97% on room air, Temp 36.6°C. Physical exam is unremarkable. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Cardiovascular exam is normal with no murmurs. Extremities show mild bilateral lower extremity edema without erythema or warmth. CBC shows mild thrombocytosis. CMP is within normal limits. Chest x-ray is clear.


A: 1. Post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), also known as long COVID. Symptoms persist > 12 weeks following initial infection. Given the exertional dyspnea and post-exertional malaise, outpatient cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) are ordered to rule out cardiac or pulmonary microvascular involvement. 2. Varicose veins, bilateral lower extremities.


P: 1. Reinforce activity pacing to avoid PEM. Work with occupational therapy on a graded exercise/activity plan. Monitor symptoms weekly using a symptom diary. Consider referral to pulmonary rehabilitation. 2. Await TTE and CPET results before initiating any disease-modifying therapy. 3. Continue electrolyte and hydration optimization given reported edema and fatigue. 4. Return to clinic in 2 weeks to review initial workup.
